correspondences.note_fr: L’article 11 impose la coopération aux mesures d’instruction, autorise la production forcée de documents détenus par une partie ou un tiers et permet des conséquences en cas de refus. Les Rules 58.01 et 58.02 organisent la production par les parties et les tiers, tandis que la Rule 61.01 prévoit les sanctions, avec des modalités distinctes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 11 requires cooperation with investigative measures, allows compelled production from parties or non-parties, and permits consequences for refusal. Rules 58.01 and 58.02 regulate production by parties and non-parties, while Rule 61.01 provides sanctions, subject to different procedures and conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet à une partie de demander au juge d’ordonner à un tiers la délivrance ou la production d’un acte ou d’une pièce. Les Rules 58.02 et 57.09 prévoient plutôt une subpoena adressée au non-party, avec production forcée et possibilité de contrôle judiciaire; la technique diffère, mais la fonction est comparable.
correspondences.note_en: The article allows a party to ask the court to order a non-party to deliver or produce an instrument or document. Rules 58.02 and 57.09 instead use a subpoena directed to the non-party, with compelled production and judicial control; the technique differs, but the function is comparable.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut ordonner la production en original, copie ou extrait, fixer les modalités et assortir l’ordre d’une astreinte. Les Rules 58.02 et 57.09 permettent la production, l’inspection et la copie, ainsi que des mesures judiciaires et le contempt, mais ne reprennent pas exactement ces modalités ni l’astreinte.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may order production of the original, a copy, or an extract, set the conditions, and attach a coercive penalty. Rules 58.02 and 57.09 allow production, inspection, and copying, together with judicial remedies and contempt, but do not reproduce these exact modalities or the French astreinte.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 243 permet au technicien de demander tous documents aux parties et aux tiers, le juge intervenant en cas de difficulté. La Rule 58.01 régit la production par les parties, la Rule 58.02 celle imposée aux non-parties par subpoena, et le RSMo 515.130 reconnaît un pouvoir documentaire aux referees; les procédures et titulaires du pouvoir diffèrent.
correspondences.note_en: Article 243 permits a technician to request documents from parties and non-parties, with judicial intervention if difficulties arise. Rule 58.01 governs production by parties, Rule 58.02 subpoenas non-parties, and RSMo 515.130 gives referees document-compulsion authority; the procedures and actors differ.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge conserve l’écrit contesté et les pièces de comparaison, ou en ordonne le dépôt au greffe. Les textes du Missouri permettent d’ordonner ou de demander la production et l’inspection de documents, mais ne prévoient pas ici leur dépôt au greffe pour vérification d’écriture.
correspondences.note_en: The judge retains the disputed writing and comparison materials or orders their filing with the clerk. Missouri provisions authorize court-ordered or requested production and inspection of documents, but do not provide for filing them with the clerk for handwriting verification.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut imposer à des tiers la remise de documents, sous astreinte, et prescrire des mesures de conservation, consultation, reproduction et restitution. Les règles du Missouri organisent la subpoena et la production par les non-parties, avec possibilité de contempt, mais ne détaillent pas toutes ces mesures de gestion documentaire.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may compel third parties to produce documents, under coercion, and prescribe preservation, inspection, copying, and return measures. Missouri rules provide subpoenas and production by non-parties, with possible contempt, but do not detail all of these document-management measures.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge de la mise en état dispose de pouvoirs généraux pour communiquer, obtenir et faire produire les pièces. Les règles du Missouri organisent la discovery et la production par les parties ou par subpoena, avec des conditions et techniques différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The juge de la mise en état has broad powers to obtain and compel production of documents. Missouri Rules 56.01 and 58.02, together with RSMo 510.030, address discovery and document production through party requests, court orders, and subpoenas, but under materially different mechanisms and conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: Le magistrat peut ordonner d’office des mesures d’instruction et imposer, sous astreinte, la production de documents par une partie ou un tiers. Rule 56.01 organise la discovery, Rule 58.02 la production par un tiers et Rule 61.01 les conséquences du défaut, mais sans reprendre exactement le pouvoir d’office ni l’astreinte.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may order investigative measures sua sponte and compel a party or nonparty to produce documents subject to a penalty. Rule 56.01 governs discovery, Rule 58.02 nonparty production, and Rule 61.01 enforcement, but none exactly reproduces the sua-sponte power or French astreinte.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1469 permet d’obtenir judiciairement la production, par un tiers, d’un acte ou d’une pièce à la suite d’une invitation du tribunal arbitral. Les Rules 58.02 et 57.09 permettent la production de documents par subpoena contre un non-partie, mais ne prévoient ni le mécanisme arbitral ni la même procédure judiciaire.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1469 permits court-ordered production by a non-party following an invitation from the arbitral tribunal. Rules 58.02 and 57.09 permit document production by subpoena from a non-party, but provide neither the arbitral mechanism nor the same court procedure.

norms.heading: Request for and Effect of Admissions

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 59 — Admission of Facts and of Genuineness of Documents

norms.text:
(a) Scope. After commencement of an action, a party may serve upon any other party no more than 25 written requests for the admission, without leave of court or stipulation of the parties, for purposes of the pending action only, of the truth of any matters within the scope of Rule 56.01(b) set forth in the request that relate to statements or opinions of fact or of the application of law to fact, including the genuineness or foundation of any documents described in the request.
However, the limitation on the number of requests for admission specified by this Rule 59.01 shall not apply to requests for admission regarding the genuineness or admissibility of documents.

(1) The request for admissions shall have included at the beginning of said request the following language in all capital letters, boldface type, and a character size that is as large as the largest character size of any other material in the request:
"A FAILURE TO TIMELY RESPOND TO REQUESTS FOR ADMISSIONS IN COMPLIANCE WITH RULE 59.01 SHALL RESULT IN EACH MATTER BEING ADMITTED BY YOU AND NOT SUBJECT TO FURTHER DISPUTE."

(2) Except in cases where the provisions of Chapter 517 apply, a failure to timely respond to requests for admissions in compliance with this Rule 59.01 shall result in each matter being admitted.
In cases where the provisions of Chapter 517 apply, upon a party's failure to timely respond to requests for admissions the court may, upon motion and reasonable notice to the parties, take such actions in regard to the failure to respond as are just, and among others the following:

(i) Grant a non-responding party additional time to respond;
(ii) Order no response be required;

(iii) Order the requests for admissions be revised, or reformatted and served again, or served again in a specific manner or place; or

(iv) Order any proper request for admission be deemed admitted in the pending action against the non-responding party.

(b) Effect of Admission. Any matter admitted under this Rule 59.01 is conclusively established unless the court on motion permits withdrawal or amendment of the admission.
Subject to the provisions of Rule 62.01 governing amendment of a pre-trial order, the court may permit withdrawal or amendment when the presentation of the merits of the action will be subserved thereby and the party who obtained the admission fails to satisfy the court that withdrawal or amendment will prejudice the party in maintaining the action or defense on the merits.
Any admission made by a party under this Rule 59.01 is for the purpose of the pending action only and is not an admission by the party for any other purpose nor may it be used against the party in any other proceeding.

(c) Issuance.

(1) Form. In consecutively numbered paragraphs, the request shall set forth each matter for which an admission is requested. Copies of documents about which admissions are requested shall be served with the request unless copies have already been furnished. The title shall identify the party to whom the request for admissions are directed and state the number of the set of requests directed to that party.
(2) When Requests May Be Served. Without leave of court, requests may be served on:

(A) A plaintiff after commencement of the action,

(B) A defendant or respondent upon the expiration of 30 days after the first event of the defendant entering an appearance or being served with process, and

(C) Any other party with or after the party was served with process, entered an appearance, or filed a pleading.
(3) Service. Copies of the requests shall be served on all parties not in default. The party issuing the requests shall also provide each responding party an electronic copy in a commonly used medium, such as a diskette, CD-ROM, or as an e-mail attachment, in a format that can be read by most commonly used word processing programs, such as Word for Windows or WordPerfect 5.x or higher. In addition to the information normally in a certificate of service, the certificate of service shall also state the:
(A) Name of each party who is to respond to the requests;

(B) Number of the set of requests; and

(C) Format of the electronic copy and the medium used to transmit the electronic copy to the responding party.

At the time of service, a certificate of service, but not the requests, shall be filed with the court as provided in Rule 59.01(d).
(d) Response. The requests shall be answered by each party to whom they are directed.

(1) When Response Is Due. Responses shall be served within 30 days after the service of the requests for admissions. A defendant or respondent, however, shall not be required to respond to requests for admissions before the expiration of 60 days after the earlier of the defendant:
(A) Entering an appearance, or

(B) Being served with process.

The court may allow a shorter or longer time.

(2) Form. The title of the response shall identify the responding party and the number of the set of the requests for admissions. The response shall quote each request, including its original paragraph number, and immediately thereunder specifically:
(A) Admit the matter;

(B) Deny the matter;

(C) Object to the matter and state each reason for the objection; or

(D) Set forth in detail the reasons why the responding party cannot truthfully admit or deny the matter.

A denial shall fairly meet the substance of the requested admission.

When good faith requires that a party qualify an answer or deny only a part of the matter of which an admission is requested, the party shall specify so much of it as true and qualify or deny the remainder.
A responding party may give lack of information or knowledge as a reason for failure to admit or deny if such party states that the party has made reasonable inquiry and the information known or readily obtainable by the party is insufficient to enable the party to admit or deny.

A party who considers that a matter of which an admission has been requested presents a genuine issue for trial may not, on that ground alone, object to the request; such party may deny the matter, subject to the provisions of Rule 61.01(c), or set forth reasons why the party cannot admit or deny it.
(3) Objections and Privileges. If an objection is asserted, then each reason for the objection shall be stated. If a failure to admit or deny a request is based on a privilege or the work product doctrine, then without revealing the protected information, the objecting party shall state information that will permit others to assess the applicability of the privilege or work product doctrine.
(4) Signing. The response shall be signed by the party or the party's attorney.

(5) Service. The party to whom the requests were directed shall serve a signed original of the response and objections, if any, on the party that issued the requests and a copy upon all parties not in default. The certificate of service shall state the name of the party who issued the requests and the number of the set of requests.
At the time of service, a certificate of service, but not the response, shall be filed with the court as provided in Rule 59.01(d).

(e) Filing Request and Responses. The request and response thereto shall not be filed with the court except upon court order or contemporaneously with a motion placing the request in issue. However, both when the request and the response are served the party serving them shall file with the court a certificate of service. Each party filing a certificate shall maintain a copy of the document that is the subject of the certificate until the case is finally disposed.
(f) Enforcement. The party who has requested the admissions may move to have determined the sufficiency of the answers or objections. Unless the court determines that an objection is proper, it shall order that an answer be served. If the court determines that an answer does not comply with the requirements of this Rule 59.01, it may order either that:
(1) The matter is admitted, or

(2) An amended answer be served.

The provisions of Rule 61.01(c) apply to the award of expenses incurred in relation to the motion.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 285 répartit la compétence pour la vérification incidente ou principale des écritures sous seing privé. Les règles 59.01 et 510.050 organisent les demandes d’admission de l’authenticité des documents, mais ne répartissent pas cette compétence entre juridictions.
correspondences.note_en: Article 285 allocates jurisdiction over incidental or principal verification of private writings. Rules 59.01 and 510.050 provide procedures for admitting the genuineness of documents, but do not allocate jurisdiction between courts.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge vérifie l’écriture ou la signature contestée, y compris électroniques, sauf inutilité. Les Rules 59.01 et RSMo 510.050 organisent surtout l’admission ou le refus de l’authenticité des documents, avec effet procédural, mais ne prévoient pas la vérification judiciaire de l’écriture elle-même.
correspondences.note_en: The court verifies disputed handwriting or signatures, including electronic ones, unless unnecessary. Rules 59.01 and RSMo 510.050 mainly provide for requests to admit or deny document genuineness and their procedural effects, but do not establish judicial handwriting verification itself.

correspondences.note_fr: Lorsque le défendeur reconnaît l'écriture, le juge en donne acte. La Rule 59.01 traite de l'admission de l'authenticité des documents et rend l'admission concluante, mais selon la procédure distincte des demandes d'admission.
correspondences.note_en: When the defendant acknowledges the handwriting, the judge records that acknowledgment. Rule 59.01 addresses admissions of document genuineness and makes them conclusive, but through the distinct requests-for-admission procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: Le déni ou la méconnaissance de l'écriture entraîne une procédure de vérification. La Rule 59.01 permet de nier l'authenticité d'un document dans le cadre de demandes d'admission, mais n'organise pas une vérification d'écriture comparable. La Rule 74.05, non retenue, concerne le défaut de plaider ou de se défendre.
correspondences.note_en: A denial or failure to recognize handwriting triggers a verification procedure. Rule 59.01 permits denial of a document’s genuineness through requests for admission, but does not establish comparable handwriting verification. Rule 74.05, not retained, concerns failure to plead or otherwise defend.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 299 organise l’examen judiciaire d’un écrit sous seing privé argué de faux en renvoyant aux articles 287 à 295. Le RSMo 510.060(3) prévoit la contestation et la preuve de l’authenticité d’un document, avec une éventuelle imputation des frais; la Rule 59.01 encadre les admissions relatives à l’authenticité, sans organiser l’incident de faux lui-même.
correspondences.note_en: Article 299 directs the court to examine a private writing alleged to be forged under Articles 287–295. RSMo 510.060(3) addresses denial and proof of a document’s genuineness, with possible costs, while Rule 59.01 governs admissions concerning genuineness but does not establish a forgery incident procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’absence du défendeur ou sa volonté d’utiliser la pièce entraîne la poursuite de la procédure de faux. Les Rules 59.01 et 61.01(c) concernent les admissions et les conséquences du défaut de réponse sur l’authenticité des documents; RSMo 517.131 prévoit, dans son champ propre, le jugement par défaut en cas de non-comparution.
correspondences.note_en: The defendant’s nonappearance or decision to use the document leads to continuation of the forgery procedure. Rules 59.01 and 61.01(c) address admissions and nonresponse concerning document genuineness; RSMo 517.131 provides, in its own setting, for default judgment after nonappearance.

norms.heading: Examination and Report

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 60 — Physical and Mental Examination of Persons

norms.text:
(a) Order for Examination.

(1) In an action in which the mental condition, physical condition, or blood relationship of a party, or of an agent or a person in the custody or under the legal control of a party, is in controversy, the court in which the action is pending may order the party

(i) to submit to physical, mental, or blood examinations by physicians or other appropriate licensed health care providers or
(ii) to produce for such examinations such party's agent or the person in such party's custody or legal control.

(2) In any action in which the vocational ability of a party, or of an agent or a person in the custody or under the legal control of a party, is in controversy, the court in which the action is pending may order the party
(i) to submit to evaluation by vocational rehabilitation professionals or

(ii) to produce for such evaluation such party's agent or the person in such party's custody or legal control.
(3) Any order under this Rule 60.01(a) may be made only on motion for good cause shown, upon notice to the person against whom the order is sought and to all other parties. Such order shall specify the time, place, manner, conditions, scope of, and identity of each person conducting the examination or evaluation. The court may, as a condition of its order, require the party requesting the order to reimburse the person who is the subject of the order for that person's reasonable round trip expenses in traveling more than sixty miles from the place of residence to the place of examination or evaluation.
(b) Report of Findings.
(1) If requested by the party against whom an order is made under Rule 60.01(a) or the person who is the subject of the order, the party obtaining the order shall deliver to the requesting person or party a copy of a detailed written report of the examiner or evaluator setting out the findings, including results of all tests made, diagnosis, and conclusions, together with like reports of all earlier examinations or evaluations of the same condition.
After delivery, the party obtaining the order shall be entitled upon request to receive from the party against whom the order is made a like report of any examination or evaluation, previously or thereafter made, of the same condition, unless, in the case of a report of examination or evaluation of a person not a party, the party shows an inability to obtain it. The court on motion shall make an order against a party requiring delivery of a report on such terms as are just; if an examiner or evaluator fails or refuses to make a report, the court may exclude the examiner's or evaluator's testimony if offered at the trial.
(2) By requesting and obtaining a report of the examination or evaluation so ordered or by taking the deposition of the examiner or evaluator, the person examined or evaluated waives any privilege the person may have in that action, or any other involving the same controversy, regarding the testimony of every other person who has examined or evaluated or may thereafter examine or evaluate the person in respect of the same mental condition, physical condition, vocational ability, or blood relationship.
(3) This Rule 60.01(b) applies to examinations made by agreement of the parties, unless the agreement expressly provides otherwise, and does not preclude discovery of a report of or the taking of a deposition of the examiner or evaluator in accordance with the provisions of any other rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article impose la remise d'un rapport écrit aux parties et attribue, dans une convention entre avocats, une valeur équivalente à celle d'un avis d'expert judiciaire. La Rule 60.01(b) prévoit la remise de rapports d'examen, y compris pour les examens convenus, et la Rule 68.01 ainsi que RSMo 452.390 organisent la remise de rapports, mais aucun ne confère exactement cette valeur probatoire à un rapport privé de technicien.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires a written report to be delivered to the parties and gives a report under an agreement between lawyers the same value as a court-appointed expert opinion. Rule 60.01(b) covers reports, including agreed examinations, and Rule 68.01 and RSMo 452.390 govern report disclosure, but none gives precisely the same evidentiary status to a privately retained technician’s report.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut vérifier personnellement les faits litigieux, procéder à des constatations ou reconstitutions et se transporter sur les lieux. Les textes du Missouri permettent une expertise physique ou mentale ordonnée par le tribunal, mais non une vérification personnelle générale du juge.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may personally verify disputed facts, make observations or reconstructions, and visit the site. Missouri provisions authorize court-ordered physical or mental examinations, but not a general personal verification by the judge.

correspondences.note_fr: Si la vérification n'est pas immédiate, le juge en fixe le lieu, le jour et l'heure, et peut désigner un membre de la formation. Les règles du Missouri traitent du lieu des actes judiciaires et imposent que les ordonnances d'examen précisent notamment le temps et le lieu, sans prévoir cette désignation.
correspondences.note_en: If verification is not immediate, the judge sets its place, date, and time and may designate a member of the panel. Missouri rules address the place of judicial acts and require examination orders to specify time and place, but do not provide the same designation mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: Le technicien doit exécuter personnellement la mission en raison de sa qualification; pour une personne morale, les personnes physiques doivent être agréées. La Rule 60.01 exige que l’ordonnance précise l’identité de chaque personne conduisant l’examen, mais ne reprend ni l’obligation générale d’exécution personnelle ni le mécanisme applicable aux personnes morales.
correspondences.note_en: The technician must personally perform the assigned mission, and a legal entity must submit its responsible individuals for approval. Rule 60.01 requires the examination order to identify each person conducting it, but does not generally impose personal performance or regulate legal-entity technicians in the same way.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article autorise toute mesure d’information sur la personnalité et les conditions de vie du mineur et de ses parents, notamment enquête éducative, examens médicaux et expertises psychologiques ou psychiatriques. Le RSMo 211.455 prévoit une enquête sociale et des évaluations, tandis que les autres textes concernent des enquêtes ou examens dans des cadres différents.
correspondences.note_en: The article authorizes inquiries into the personality and living conditions of the child and parents, including educational investigations, medical examinations, and psychological or psychiatric expertise. RSMo 211.455 provides a social investigation and evaluations; the other provisions address comparable inquiries or examinations in different procedural settings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1212 permet au juge des tutelles et au procureur de faire examiner certains majeurs par un médecin. Les textes du Missouri permettent au tribunal d’ordonner un examen physique ou mental lorsque l’état de la personne est en cause, mais exigent une motion, un motif valable et un avis, sans conférer ce pouvoir au procureur.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1212 allows the tutorship judge and prosecutor to obtain a medical examination of certain adults. Missouri permits court-ordered physical or mental examinations when a person’s condition is in controversy, but requires a motion, good cause, and notice, and does not grant the stated authority to a prosecutor.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose un certificat médical circonstancié décrivant l’altération, son évolution et ses effets sur la capacité civile, remis sous pli cacheté au juge ou au procureur. La Rule 60.01 prévoit des examens et rapports détaillés dans une action civile, mais ne prévoit ni ce certificat ni sa remise sous pli cacheté.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires a detailed medical certificate addressing impairment, prognosis, and effects on civil capacity, delivered sealed to the judge or prosecutor. Rule 60.01 provides examinations and detailed reports in a civil action, but not this certificate or its sealed delivery.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article autorise le juge à ordonner d’office ou sur demande toute mesure d’instruction, notamment une enquête sociale ou des constatations. RSMo 452.390 et 211.455 prévoient des enquêtes et rapports dans des procédures de garde ou de protection de l’enfance; Rule 60.01 vise plus spécifiquement les examens physiques ou mentaux.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits the judge to order any investigative measure, including a social inquiry or findings by a person of the judge’s choice. RSMo 452.390 and 211.455 authorize investigations and reports in custody or child-protection proceedings, while Rule 60.01 more narrowly concerns physical or mental examinations.

norms.heading: Failure to Make Discovery: Sanctions

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 61 — Enforcement of Discovery: Sanctions

norms.text:
(a) Failure to Act – Evasive or Incomplete Answers. Any failure to act described in this Rule 61 may not be excused on the ground that the discovery sought is objectionable unless the party failing to act has served timely objections to the discovery request or has applied for a protective order as provided by Rule 56.01(c).
For the purpose of this Rule 61, an evasive or incomplete answer is to be treated as a failure to answer.

(b) Failure to Answer Interrogatories. If a party fails to answer interrogatories or serve objections thereto within the time provided by law, or if objections are served thereto that are thereafter overruled and the interrogatories are not timely answered, the court may, upon motion and reasonable notice to other parties, take such action in regard to the failure as are just and among others the following:
(1) Enter an order striking pleadings or parts thereof or dismissing the action or proceeding or any part thereof or render a judgment by default against the disobedient party;

(2) Upon the showing of reasonable excuse, grant the party failing to answer the interrogatories additional time to serve answers, but such order shall provide that if the party fails to answer the interrogatories within the additional time allowed, the pleadings of such party shall be stricken or the action shall be dismissed or that a default judgment shall be rendered against the disobedient party.
(c) Failure to Answer Request for Admissions. If a party, after being served with a request to admit the genuineness of any relevant documents or the truth of any relevant and material matters of fact, fails to serve answers or objections thereto, as required by Rule 59.01, the genuineness of any relevant documents or the truth of any relevant and material matters of fact contained in the request for admissions shall be taken as admitted, except in cases where the provisions of Chapter 517 apply.
In such cases, where the non-answering party has failed to serve proper answers or objections thereto, such admissions shall not be deemed admitted unless the court has granted such relief pursuant to Rule 59.01(a) or Rule 59.01(f).
If a party fails to admit the genuineness of any document or the truth of any matter as requested under Rule 59.01, and if the party requesting the admissions thereafter proves the genuineness of the document or the truth of the matter, the party requesting the admissions may apply to the court for an order requiring the other party to pay the reasonable expenses incurred in making that proof, including reasonable attorney fees. The court shall make the order unless it finds that:
(1) The request was held objectionable pursuant to Rule 59.01;

(2) The admission sought was of no substantial importance;

(3) The party failing to admit had reasonable grounds to believe that such party might prevail on the matter; or

(4) There was other good reason for the failure to admit
(d) Failure to Produce Documents, and Things or to Permit Inspection. If a party fails to respond that inspection will be permitted as requested, fails to permit inspection, or fails to produce documents and tangible things as requested under Rule 58.01, or timely serves objections thereto that are thereafter overruled and the documents and things are not timely produced or inspection thereafter is not timely permitted, the court may, upon motion and reasonable notice to other parties, take such action in regard to the failure as are just and among others the following:
(1) Enter an order refusing to allow the disobedient party to support or oppose designated claims or defenses or prohibiting the disobedient party from introducing designated matters in evidence;

(2) Enter an order striking pleadings or parts thereof or staying further proceedings until the order is obeyed or dismissing the action or proceeding or any part thereof or render a judgment by default against the disobedient party;
(3) Enter an order treating as a contempt of court the failure to obey; or

(4) Enter an order requiring the party failing to obey the order or the attorney advising the party or both to pay the reasonable expenses, including attorney fees, caused by the failure unless the court finds that the failure was substantially justified or that other circumstances make an award of expenses unjust.
(e) Failure to Appear for Physical Examination. If a party fails to obey an order directing a physical or mental or blood examination under Rule 60.01, the court may, upon motion and reasonable notice to the other parties and all persons affected thereby, make such orders in regard to the failure as are just, and among others, it may take any action authorized under Rules 61.01(d)(1), (2), and (4).
Where a party has failed to comply with an order requiring the production of another for examination, the court may enter such orders as are authorized by this Rule 61.01, unless the party failing to comply shows an inability to produce such person for examination.
(f) Failure to Attend Own Deposition.
If a party, or an officer, director, managing agent of a party, or person designated under Rules 57.03(b)(4) and 57.04(a) to testify on behalf of a party, fails to appear before the officer who is to take his or her deposition, after being served with notice
, the court may, upon motion and reasonable notice to the other parties and all persons affected thereby, make such orders in regard to the failure as are just and among others, it may take any action authorized under paragraphs (1), (2), (3), and (4) of subdivision (d) of this Rule.
(g) Failure to Answer Questions on Deposition. If a witness fails or refuses to testify in response to questions propounded on deposition, the proponent of the question may move for an order compelling an answer. The proponent of the question may complete or adjourn the deposition examination before applying for an order. In ruling upon the motion, the court may make such protective order as it would have been empowered to make on a motion pursuant to Rule 56.01(c).
If the motion is granted, the court, after opportunity for hearing, shall require the party or deponent whose conduct necessitated the motion or the party or attorney advising such conduct or both of them to pay to the moving party the reasonable expenses incurred in obtaining the order, including attorney fees, unless the court finds that the opposition to the motion was substantially justified or that other circumstances make an award of expenses unjust.
If the motion is denied, the court, after opportunity for hearing, shall require the moving party or the attorney advising the motion or both of them to pay to the party or deponent who opposed the motion the reasonable expenses incurred in opposing the motion, including attorney fees, unless the court finds that the making of the motion was substantially justified or that other circumstances make an award of expenses unjust.
If the motion is granted in part and denied in part, the court may apportion the reasonable expenses incurred in relation to the motion among the parties and persons in a just manner.

If the motion is granted and if the persons ordered to respond fail to comply with the court's order, the court, upon motion and reasonable notice to the other parties and all persons affected thereby, may make such orders in regard to the failure as are just, and among others, it may take any action authorized under Rule 61.01(d).
(h) Objections to Approved Discovery. If objections to Rule 56.01(b)(8) approved interrogatories or requests for production are overruled, the court may assess against such objecting party, attorney, or attorney's law firm, or all of them, the attorney fees reasonably incurred in having such objection overruled. If such fees are not paid within 60 days, the court may enter such other appropriate orders against the disobedient party, including an order striking pleadings, dismissing the action, or entering a judgment by default.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 11 impose la coopération aux mesures d’instruction, autorise la production forcée de documents détenus par une partie ou un tiers et permet des conséquences en cas de refus. Les Rules 58.01 et 58.02 organisent la production par les parties et les tiers, tandis que la Rule 61.01 prévoit les sanctions, avec des modalités distinctes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 11 requires cooperation with investigative measures, allows compelled production from parties or non-parties, and permits consequences for refusal. Rules 58.01 and 58.02 regulate production by parties and non-parties, while Rule 61.01 provides sanctions, subject to different procedures and conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: Les parties doivent communiquer les documents nécessaires au technicien, et le juge peut en ordonner la production sous astreinte. Le Missouri prévoit le pouvoir d’un referee d’exiger des documents, ainsi que des mesures de contrainte et sanctions pour défaut de production, mais ne reprend ni l’astreinte ni la faculté expresse pour le technicien de poursuivre sur les seuls éléments disponibles.
correspondences.note_en: The parties must provide documents needed by the technician, and the judge may compel production, including under a penalty. Missouri authorizes referees to require documents and provides compulsion and sanctions for nonproduction, but does not include the French penalty mechanism or the technician’s express ability to proceed on available materials.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article permet de demander au juge, sans forme, d'enjoindre la communication non effectuée. Le Missouri prévoit une demande de production et une motion visant à obtenir une ordonnance de contrainte, généralement avec des exigences procédurales et un préavis.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits an informal request for a judicial order compelling missing disclosure. Missouri provides document requests and motions to compel or enforce production, generally subject to specified procedural requirements and notice.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article permet au juge de fixer le délai et les modalités de communication, éventuellement sous astreinte. RSMo 510.030 prévoit que l'ordonnance précise le temps, le lieu et les modalités; les règles de discovery organisent les délais et sanctions, mais pas une astreinte équivalente.
correspondences.note_en: The article authorizes the judge to set the deadline and method of disclosure, potentially backed by a coercive penalty. RSMo 510.030 requires an order to specify time, place, and manner; discovery rules provide deadlines and sanctions but no equivalent astreinte.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut écarter les pièces communiquées tardivement. La Rule 61.01(d)(1) permet d'interdire à une partie de produire certains éléments en preuve en cas de manquement à la production de documents, mais ne vise pas spécifiquement la communication tardive.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may exclude exhibits disclosed too late. Rule 61.01(d)(1) allows the court to bar a disobedient party from introducing designated matters in evidence for failure to produce documents, but it does not specifically address late disclosure.

correspondences.note_fr: Les difficultés d'exécution sont réglées par le juge compétent, à la demande des parties, du technicien ou d'office. La Rule 61.01 prévoit des mesures judiciaires en cas de non-exécution d'une mesure de découverte, la Rule 60.01 organise l'exécution des examens, et la Rule 68.03(d) la conduite des opérations du master.
correspondences.note_en: Execution difficulties are resolved by the responsible judge on a party's, technician's, or the court's own initiative. Rule 61.01 provides judicial responses to failures in discovery, Rule 60.01 structures examinations, and Rule 68.03(d) regulates a master's proceedings.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut tirer des conséquences juridiques des déclarations, de l’absence ou du refus de répondre, et assimiler ces éléments à un commencement de preuve par écrit. Les textes du Missouri autorisent surtout une inférence défavorable ou des sanctions procédurales, dans des procédures ou contextes plus limités.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may draw legal consequences from statements, absence, or refusal to answer, and treat them as equivalent to a beginning of written proof. Missouri provisions mainly authorize adverse inferences or procedural sanctions, in more limited proceedings or contexts.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 275 impose la remise à l’expert des documents nécessaires et permet au juge d’en ordonner la production, avec des conséquences en cas de carence. Les Rules 58.01 et 61.01 prévoient respectivement la production et les sanctions en cas de non-respect. Le RSMo 510.030 prévoit la production sur ordonnance, sans sanction dans le texte fourni. Ces mécanismes ne sont pas spécifiques à l’expertise.
correspondences.note_en: Article 275 requires parties to provide necessary documents to the expert and permits an order compelling production, with consequences for noncompliance. Rules 58.01 and 61.01 address production and sanctions, respectively. RSMo 510.030 authorizes production by court order but states no sanction in the supplied text. None is expert-specific.

correspondences.note_fr: L’absence du défendeur ou sa volonté d’utiliser la pièce entraîne la poursuite de la procédure de faux. Les Rules 59.01 et 61.01(c) concernent les admissions et les conséquences du défaut de réponse sur l’authenticité des documents; RSMo 517.131 prévoit, dans son champ propre, le jugement par défaut en cas de non-comparution.
correspondences.note_en: The defendant’s nonappearance or decision to use the document leads to continuation of the forgery procedure. Rules 59.01 and 61.01(c) address admissions and nonresponse concerning document genuineness; RSMo 517.131 provides, in its own setting, for default judgment after nonappearance.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut demander des explications et ordonner la production de documents, puis tirer des conséquences de l'abstention ou du refus. Les Rules 58.01 et 61.01 organisent la production et les sanctions, tandis que la Rule 62.01 permet au juge de diriger une conférence de gestion, mais aucune ne reprend exactement ce pouvoir général exercé d'office.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may request explanations, order production of documents, and draw consequences from noncompliance. Rules 58.01 and 61.01 address production and sanctions, while Rule 62.01 permits court-directed case management; none reproduces the same general sua sponte power.

correspondences.note_fr: Les règles du Missouri organisent la discovery, les mesures prises en cas de défaut de production ou de réponse, ainsi que les demandes d'honoraires. Elles ne confèrent pas l'ensemble des pouvoirs du juge français et ne prévoient pas la constatation de l'extinction de l'instance.
correspondences.note_en: Missouri rules address discovery, responses to failures to produce or answer, and attorney-fee motions. They do not confer the French judge’s complete combination of powers or provide for determining that the action has ended.

correspondences.note_fr: Le magistrat peut ordonner d’office des mesures d’instruction et imposer, sous astreinte, la production de documents par une partie ou un tiers. Rule 56.01 organise la discovery, Rule 58.02 la production par un tiers et Rule 61.01 les conséquences du défaut, mais sans reprendre exactement le pouvoir d’office ni l’astreinte.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may order investigative measures sua sponte and compel a party or nonparty to produce documents subject to a penalty. Rule 56.01 governs discovery, Rule 58.02 nonparty production, and Rule 61.01 enforcement, but none exactly reproduces the sua-sponte power or French astreinte.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise l’instruction arbitrale, l’audition de personnes et la production forcée de pièces sous astreinte. Les Rules 56.01, 58.01 et 57.03 offrent des mécanismes judiciaires comparables de découverte, de production et de déposition; la Rule 61.01 prévoit des sanctions, mais dans un cadre et selon des effets différents.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs arbitral investigation, witness hearing, and compelled production subject to a coercive penalty. Rules 56.01, 58.01, and 57.03 provide comparable court-discovery, production, and deposition mechanisms; Rule 61.01 supplies enforcement sanctions, but in a different setting and with different effects.

Rule 62 — Pre-Trial Conferences

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 8 permet au juge de demander aux parties les explications de fait nécessaires. Les dispositions Missouri prévoient des conférences dirigées par le tribunal pouvant notamment simplifier les questions et favoriser la clarification des faits et des documents.
correspondences.note_en: Article 8 permits the judge to request factual explanations needed to resolve the dispute. The Missouri provisions authorize court-directed conferences addressing simplification of issues and admissions concerning facts and documents, serving a comparable case-management function.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 128 énumère diverses conventions de mise en état, notamment sur la limitation du débat, les échanges, les techniciens et la consignation des auditions et témoignages. Les règles du Missouri couvrent séparément la gestion de l'instance, la discovery, les dépositions et la production de documents, mais sans organiser ce régime conventionnel global.
correspondences.note_en: Article 128 lists party agreements concerning issues, exchanges, experts, examinations, and witness statements. The Missouri provisions separately address case management, discovery, depositions, and document production, but do not create the same comprehensive contractual case-preparation framework.

correspondences.note_fr: Après l’exécution de la mesure, l’instance se poursuit sous la diligence du juge, qui peut entendre immédiatement les parties et statuer. La Rule 55.30 organise les audiences et la décision sur les demandes, tandis que la Rule 62.01 permet au juge de gérer la suite de l’instance, sans prévoir spécifiquement cette situation.
correspondences.note_en: After the evidentiary measure is completed, the case proceeds under the judge’s direction, who may immediately hear the parties and rule. Rule 55.30 governs hearings and determination of matters, while Rule 62.01 permits judicial management of the case, but neither specifically addresses completion of an evidentiary measure.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut ordonner la comparution personnelle des parties, en toute matière. La Rule 62.01 permet au tribunal d’ordonner aux parties de comparaître à une conférence de gestion, tandis que le RSMo 452.830 prévoit une comparution ordonnée dans le cadre limité d’une procédure de garde d’enfants sur demande d’un autre État.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may order the parties, or one of them, to appear personally in any matter. Rule 62.01 permits the court to direct parties to appear at a case-management conference, and RSMo 452.830 permits an appearance order in the narrower context of an interstate custody proceeding.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 264 pose le principe de la désignation d’un seul expert, sauf nécessité d’en nommer plusieurs. La Rule 62.01 permet au tribunal de limiter le nombre d’experts, mais ne règle pas directement leur désignation judiciaire.
correspondences.note_en: Article 264 establishes a one-expert rule unless several are necessary. Rule 62.01 permits the court to limit the number of expert witnesses, but does not directly govern court appointment of experts.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 266 permet une conférence destinée à préciser la mission et le calendrier, ainsi que la remise de documents à l’expert. La Rule 62.01 prévoit une conférence pouvant porter sur les experts et leur calendrier, mais aucune disposition citée ne règle précisément la clarification de la mission ou la remise des documents à l’expert.
correspondences.note_en: Article 266 permits a conference to clarify the expert’s assignment and schedule and to provide documents to the expert. Rule 62.01 allows a conference concerning experts and timing, but none of the cited provisions specifically governs clarification of the assignment or delivery of documents to the expert.

correspondences.note_fr: Le CPC permet au juge d’organiser les échanges, d’en fixer les délais et modalités, et d’écarter les communications tardives portant atteinte aux droits de la défense. La Rule 62.01 permet une gestion judiciaire contraignante de l’instance, tandis que la Rule 43.01 régit la communication des actes, sans prévoir l’ensemble des sanctions et mécanismes du CPC.
correspondences.note_en: The CPC authorizes judicial organization of party exchanges, deadlines, and methods, including exclusion of late submissions that prejudice the defense. Rule 62.01 provides binding case-management orders, and Rule 43.01 governs service, but neither reproduces all of the CPC’s exchange mechanisms and sanctions.

correspondences.note_fr: Le président entend les avocats sur l'état de l'affaire et leur demande notamment s'ils envisagent une convention de mise en état. Les textes du Missouri prévoient une conférence de gestion examinant diverses questions procédurales, mais elle est facultative et ne vise pas spécifiquement cette convention.
correspondences.note_en: The president consults counsel about the procedural posture and specifically asks whether they contemplate a case-management agreement. The Missouri provisions allow a case-management conference addressing various procedural matters, but the conference is discretionary and does not specifically concern such an agreement.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 779 organise une ultime conférence d’orientation, les derniers échanges, la clôture de l’instruction ou le renvoi au juge de la mise en état, avec fixation d’audiences. Les Rules 62.01 et RSMo 510.010 prévoient des conférences de gestion et un ordre procédural, mais sans reprendre tout ce mécanisme; les autres dispositions concernent surtout les continuations et la fixation du procès.
correspondences.note_en: Article 779 governs a final case-orientation conference, last submissions, closing of the proceedings, or referral to the judge for case management, with hearings set as needed. Rules 62.01 and RSMo 510.010 provide comparable case-management conferences and controlling orders, but do not reproduce the full mechanism; the other provisions address continuances and trial settings.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge de la mise en état surveille loyalement l’instruction, peut communiquer avec les avocats, leur adresser des injonctions et ordonner le retrait du rôle. La Rule 62.01 prévoit une conférence de gestion et une ordonnance contrôlant la suite de l’instance, mais pas ce rôle permanent ni le retrait du rôle.
correspondences.note_en: The French judge supervises the orderly conduct of the proceedings, may communicate with and direct counsel, and may order removal from the docket. Rule 62.01 provides case-management conferences and an order controlling the action, but not the same continuing role or docket withdrawal.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge fixe les délais d’instruction, peut les proroger et établir un calendrier comprenant les échanges, la clôture, les débats et le prononcé. La Rule 62.01 permet de régler la séquence et le calendrier de certaines étapes, tandis que RSMo 517.071 traite de la continuation et du rééchelonnement, dans un cadre plus limité.
correspondences.note_en: The judge sets procedural deadlines, may extend them, and may establish a timetable for submissions, closure, hearing, and judgment. Rule 62.01 addresses sequencing and timing of case-management matters, while RSMo 517.071 governs continuances and rescheduling in a narrower setting.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut inviter les avocats à compléter leurs moyens et explications, à mettre leurs écritures en conformité et à communiquer les originaux ou copies des pièces. La Rule 62.01 permet de simplifier les questions, et la Rule 56.01 organise la production et l’obtention de documents, sans reprendre exactement ces pouvoirs du juge de la mise en état.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may require counsel to address undeveloped arguments, provide necessary factual and legal explanations, conform pleadings, and produce original or copied exhibits. Rule 62.01 concerns issue simplification, and Rule 56.01 governs document discovery, but neither reproduces these exact case-management powers.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article attribue au juge de la mise en état une compétence exclusive sur les exceptions, incidents, mesures provisoires et mesures d'instruction, ainsi que sur les fins de non-recevoir. Rule 55.27 et Rule 67.03 couvrent certaines contestations et décisions préalables, tandis que Rule 62.01 traite de la gestion préalable, sans équivalent global à cette compétence exclusive.
correspondences.note_en: This article gives the case-management judge exclusive authority over defenses, terminating incidents, provisional and evidentiary measures, and objections to admissibility. Rule 55.27 and Rule 67.03 cover some pretrial defenses and dismissals, while Rule 62.01 concerns case management; none reproduces the overall exclusive jurisdiction.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 799 organise la clôture de l’instruction, le renvoi au procès, la fixation de la date et, avec l’accord des parties, le dépôt des dossiers sans audience. Les règles 62.01, 63.01 et 63.02 concernent la gestion et la fixation du procès, tandis que la règle 55.30 permet une décision écrite sans débat oral.
correspondences.note_en: Article 799 governs closing the case preparation, setting trial, and—by agreement—submitting papers without a hearing. Rules 62.01, 63.01, and 63.02 address case management and trial settings, while Rule 55.30 permits submission without oral argument, but none reproduces the French mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge organise les échanges entre les parties et peut les dispenser de comparaître ultérieurement, avec les sanctions prévues. La Rule 62.01 permet une gestion judiciaire de l’instance et fixe les mesures de préparation, mais ne prévoit ni exactement ces échanges ni cette dispense de comparution.
correspondences.note_en: The judge organizes party exchanges and may excuse a party from a later hearing, subject to specified sanctions. Rule 62.01 permits judicial case management and sets pretrial measures, but does not provide the same exchange procedure or excusal mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut entendre les parties et exerce les pouvoirs de mise en état prévus par l’article 446-3. La Rule 62.01 prévoit la gestion de l’instance et la Rule 56.01 encadre la découverte, mais aucune ne confère exactement l’ensemble de ces pouvoirs au juge instructeur.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may hear the parties and exercise broad case-preparation powers. Rule 62.01 provides case management, while Rule 56.01 regulates discovery, but neither grants precisely the same powers to an assigned instructing judge.

correspondences.note_fr: Le conseiller peut entendre les avocats ou les parties contradictoirement et inviter à mettre en cause les intéressés nécessaires. La Rule 55.30 organise les audiences et certaines modalités de participation, tandis que la Rule 62.01 prévoit une conférence de gestion avec les parties; aucune ne reprend exactement les garanties et pouvoirs du texte français.
correspondences.note_en: The French rule permits hearings of counsel or parties on a contradictory basis and allows necessary interested persons to be joined. Rule 55.30 governs hearings and participation methods, and Rule 62.01 provides case-management conferences with the parties, but neither reproduces the French safeguards and joinder power exactly.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 914-2 sanctionne le défaut d’accomplissement des actes prévus au calendrier par une clôture partielle, prévoit sa rétractation dans certains cas et permet la clôture finale. La Rule 62.01 donne force obligatoire aux ordres de gestion; les Rules 84.08 et 61.01 prévoient d’autres conséquences procédurales en cas de défaut, notamment le rejet ou des sanctions.
correspondences.note_en: Article 914-2 sanctions failure to perform acts required by a case-management schedule through partial closure, allows limited retraction, and provides for final closure. Rule 62.01 gives case-management orders controlling effect; Rules 84.08 and 61.01 provide different procedural consequences for defaults, including dismissal or sanctions.

norms.heading: Trial Settings – Single-Judge Circuits

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 63 — Trial Settings

norms.text:
In all single-judge circuits, orders setting civil actions for trial shall be made:

(1) Upon the court's own motion, on the first day of any term of court; or

(2) Upon the court's own motion on any regularly scheduled law day, if five days' written notice (stating the date upon which such order setting the case for trial is to be entered) has been given by the court to all parties; or

(3) At any time when there is agreement of all parties; or

(4) Upon request of any party, when the issues have been joined and a reasonable time has elapsed for discovery, if five days' written notice (stating the date upon which such order setting the civil action for trial shall be requested) has been given by the requesting party to all other parties.

committee_notes:
Committee Note – 1974

This is new and is a substantial change from prior Rule 63.01.

correspondences.note_fr: Rule 63.01 traite de la fixation des affaires civiles pour l'audience, et Rule 43.02 du dépôt des actes au tribunal. Aucun de ces textes ne prévoit la convention participative, l'information spécifique du juge ni le mécanisme de clôture de l'instruction.
correspondences.note_en: Rule 63.01 addresses setting civil actions for trial, and Rule 43.02 addresses filing papers with the court. Neither provides for the participatory agreement, specific notice to the judge, or the case-preparation closure mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe le jour et l’heure des débats, permet leur poursuite à une audience ultérieure et exige leur reprise en cas de changement de composition. Les règles du Missouri traitent de la fixation des audiences et des ajournements, mais non de la reprise obligatoire due au changement de composition.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs the scheduling and continuation of hearings and requires hearings to begin again if the court’s composition changes. The Missouri rules address hearing and trial settings and continuances, but not mandatory recommencement after a change in composition.

correspondences.note_fr: Le président renvoie les affaires en état à l'audience, clôt l'instruction et fixe la date de plaidoirie, avec une procédure particulière en cas de jugement sans audience. Les textes du Missouri régissent la mise au rôle et la fixation du procès, mais ne prévoient pas l'ensemble de ces mécanismes ni la clôture française de l'instruction.
correspondences.note_en: The president sends trial-ready cases to the hearing, closes the preparatory phase, and sets the trial date, with a special procedure for determination without a hearing. The Missouri provisions govern docketing and trial settings, but do not provide all of these mechanisms or the French form of closing the proceedings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 799 organise la clôture de l’instruction, le renvoi au procès, la fixation de la date et, avec l’accord des parties, le dépôt des dossiers sans audience. Les règles 62.01, 63.01 et 63.02 concernent la gestion et la fixation du procès, tandis que la règle 55.30 permet une décision écrite sans débat oral.
correspondences.note_en: Article 799 governs closing the case preparation, setting trial, and—by agreement—submitting papers without a hearing. Rules 62.01, 63.01, and 63.02 address case management and trial settings, while Rule 55.30 permits submission without oral argument, but none reproduces the French mechanism.

correspondences.note_en: Article 377 provides that proceedings are suspended by an order staying, striking, or removing the case from the docket, unless otherwise provided by law. Missouri provides stays or continuances in specific contexts and subject to particular conditions, but does not generally reproduce all three mechanisms.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe le jour et l’heure des débats, permet leur poursuite à une audience ultérieure et exige leur reprise en cas de changement de composition. correspondences.note_en: The article governs the scheduling and continuation of hearings and requires hearings to begin again if the court’s composition changes. The Missouri rules address hearing and trial settings and continuances, but not mandatory recommencement after a change in composition.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 468 prévoit les effets de la non-comparution injustifiée du demandeur : jugement au fond, renvoi, caducité de la citation et relevé de caducité sous quinze jours. La Rule 67.03 permet le rejet pour défaut de poursuite ou de respect des règles, la Rule 74.05 le jugement par défaut, et la Rule 65.01 le renvoi, mais aucune ne reprend l’ensemble de ce régime.
correspondences.note_en: Article 468 addresses the plaintiff’s unjustified failure to appear, allowing a merits judgment, continuance, dismissal for lapse of the summons, and reinstatement within fifteen days. Rule 67.03 permits dismissal for failure to prosecute or comply, Rule 74.05 permits default judgment, and Rule 65.01 permits continuances, but none reproduces the full regime.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 830 prévoit le jugement immédiat à défaut de conciliation ou le renvoi à une audience ultérieure, avec information des parties par le greffe. correspondences.note_en: Article 830 provides for immediate judgment after failed conciliation or adjournment to a later hearing, with clerk notice to the parties. Rule 65.01 permits continuance to a fixed date, and Rule 43.01 governs transmission of notices and documents, but neither reproduces the full procedural sequence.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit le renvoi de l’affaire à une audience ultérieure et l’information des parties sur les audiences suivantes. correspondences.note_en: The article provides for continuation to a later hearing and notice of subsequent hearings. Rules 65.01 and 55.30 and RSMo 510.080 address continuances and hearing arrangements, but do not reproduce the full French mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: Le tribunal arbitral peut suspendre l’instance pour une durée ou jusqu’à un événement, puis révoquer ou abréger le sursis. correspondences.note_en: An arbitral tribunal may stay proceedings for a specified period or until an event, and may revoke or shorten the stay. The Missouri provisions provide comparable stays or continuances, but only in specified judicial contexts and without the same general arbitral power.

norms.heading: Consolidation

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

Rule 66 — Consolidation of Civil Actions and Separate Trials

norms.text:
(a) Consolidation – Same Parties. Whenever several civil actions founded alone upon liquidated demands shall be pending in the same court by the same plaintiff against the same defendant, or whenever several such civil actions are pending in the same court by the same plaintiff against several defendants, the court in which the same shall be prosecuted may, in its discretion, if it appear expedient, order such civil actions to be consolidated into one civil action.
(b) Consolidation – Common Question of Law or Fact. When civil actions involving a common question of law or fact are pending before the court, it may order a joint hearing or trial of any or all the matters in issue in the civil actions; it may order all the civil actions consolidated; and it may make such orders concerning proceedings therein as may tend to avoid unnecessary costs or delay.
(c) Consolidation – Family Court Matters. When more than one civil action pending in the family court division of the circuit court involves the same or different members of the same family, the administrative judge of the division may assign all such actions to any judge within the division. The judge to whom the actions are assigned may consolidate any or all of such actions as may be appropriate.
(d) Consolidation – Injury to Spouse. If an injury not resulting in death is inflicted upon the person of one spouse, and causes of action therefor accrue to the injured spouse and also to the other spouse for loss of consortium or services or medical expenses, they shall be enforced in one action by both spouses if they have ever been coparties in such action or if notice is given.
If any party against whom a claim is asserted gives written notice of the pendency of the action and of the necessity to join therein to the spouse whose claim was not joined and to the attorney for the spouse upon whose behalf the lawsuit was filed, the claim of such spouse who has not been joined shall be barred unless the spouse makes application to be added as a party therein within thirty days after such notice. The spouse so required to join shall have an unconditional right to be added as a party pursuant to Rule 52.06.
(e) Notice – How Given. The notice shall be given to the attorney by first class mail, postage prepaid. The notice shall be given to the party:

1. By personal service within or without this state with proof thereof by the return of the officer or by affidavit; or

2. By registered or certified mail, requesting a receipt signed by addressee only, with proof thereof by the filing of the United States Postal Service receipt signed by such person.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge de la mise en état ordonne les jonctions et disjonctions d'instance. Les Rules 66.01 et 66.02, ainsi que le RSMo 510.180, prévoient respectivement la consolidation d'actions et la tenue de procès séparés, mais avec des conditions et effets plus détaillés.
correspondences.note_en: The juge de la mise en état orders the consolidation or severance of proceedings. Rules 66.01 and 66.02, and RSMo 510.180, respectively provide for consolidation and separate trials, but with more detailed conditions and effects.

correspondences.note_en: The assigned judge conducts consolidation and severance of proceedings. Missouri provisions allow the court to consolidate actions and order separate trials, but do not establish a French-style pretrial judge or an identical severance mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 913-3 attribue au conseiller de la mise en état les jonctions et disjonctions d’instance, le retrait du rôle et certaines décisions sur les dépens et l’article 700. correspondences.note_fr: Le magistrat tranche les difficultés de communication des pièces et ordonne les jonctions ou disjonctions d’instance. Rule 66.01 traite de la consolidation, tandis que Rule 81.15 permet de régler des contestations relatives au contenu du dossier d’appel, sans couvrir directement la communication des pièces.
correspondences.note_en: The assigned judge resolves disputes about communicating exhibits and orders consolidation or severance. Rule 66.01 addresses consolidation, while Rule 81.15 permits resolution of disputes about the appellate record, but neither directly covers exhibit communication.

La Rule 66.02 autorise un procès séparé et la Rule 74.01(b) un jugement portant sur moins que toutes les demandes, mais aucune ne reprend exactement ce mécanisme de césure consensuelle.
correspondences.note_en: The article allows all parties to request partial closure so that specified claims may be adjudicated while the remainder continues. Rule 66.02 permits separate trials and Rule 74.01(b) permits judgment on fewer than all claims, but neither reproduces the consensual partial-closure mechanism exactly.

norms.text: A dismissal without prejudice permits the party to bring another civil action for the same cause, unless the civil action is otherwise barred. A dismissal with prejudice bars the assertion of the same cause of action or claim against the same party.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 385 énumère les causes d’extinction principale de l’instance—péremption, désistement d’instance et caducité de la citation—et préserve la possibilité d’une nouvelle instance si l’action subsiste. Les Rules 67.01 à 67.03 organisent les dismissals, notamment sans préjudice et avec possibilité de réintroduire l’action, mais ne couvrent pas exactement toutes les causes françaises ni le dessaisissement correspondant.
correspondences.note_en: Article 385 lists principal grounds for terminating a proceeding—lapse, withdrawal of the proceeding, and nullity or expiration of the summons—while preserving a new action if the claim survives. Rules 67.01–67.03 provide dismissals, often without prejudice and allowing refiling, but do not match all French grounds or the corresponding divestiture mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: La péremption éteint l’instance sans éteindre l’action et interdit de se prévaloir des actes de l’instance périmée. Les règles du Missouri organisent des dismissals, notamment pour défaut de poursuite, dont l’effet peut être sans préjudice, mais sans reprendre exactement cette règle sur les actes antérieurs.
correspondences.note_en: Lapse terminates the proceeding without extinguishing the claim and prevents reliance on acts in the lapsed proceeding. Missouri rules provide dismissals, including for failure to prosecute, which may be without prejudice, but do not reproduce the specific rule concerning prior procedural acts.

correspondences.note_fr: Le désistement éteint l’instance sans renoncer à l’action. Les dismissals without prejudice du Missouri permettent d’engager une nouvelle action pour la même cause, sous réserve des règles applicables et de certaines limites procédurales.
correspondences.note_en: Withdrawal ends the proceeding without waiving the underlying action. Missouri dismissals without prejudice permit another action for the same cause, subject to applicable bars and procedural limitations.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge constate l’extinction de l’instance, sans préciser ici le mode d’extinction. Les Rules 67.02 et 67.03 organisent la cessation de l’action par dismissal, et la Rule 67.01 en précise les effets, mais selon une technique et des conditions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The judge records the termination of the proceedings without specifying the particular mode of termination. Rules 67.02 and 67.03 provide for termination through dismissal, and Rule 67.01 states its effects, but by a different mechanism and under different conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit l’extinction de l’instance en cas de non-comparution ou de défaut de constitution d’avocat et rend non avenue l’ordonnance. Les textes du Missouri permettent le rejet et en précisent les effets, mais ne prévoient pas cette extinction ni l’anéantissement de l’ordonnance.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides for termination when the parties fail to appear or the creditor fails to obtain counsel, and renders the payment order ineffective. Missouri provisions allow dismissal and specify its effects, but do not provide for this specific termination or nullification of the order.

norms.heading: Voluntary Dismissal – Effect of

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 67 — Dismissal of Civil Actions

norms.text:
(a) Except as provided in Rule 52, a civil action may be dismissed by the plaintiff without order of the court anytime:

(1) Prior to the swearing of the jury panel for the voir dire examination, or

(2) In cases tried without a jury, prior to the introduction of evidence at the trial.
A party who once so dismisses a civil action and thereafter files another civil action upon the same claim shall be allowed to dismiss the same without prejudice only:

(1) Upon filing a stipulation to that effect signed by the opposing party, or

(2) On order of the court made on motion in which the ground for dismissal shall be set forth.
(b) Except as provided in Rule 67.02(a), an action shall not be dismissed at the plaintiff's instance except upon order of the court upon such terms and conditions as the court deems proper.

(c) A voluntary dismissal under Rule 67.02(a) shall be without prejudice unless otherwise specified by the plaintiff. Any other voluntary dismissal shall be without prejudice unless otherwise specified by the court or the parties to the dismissal.
(d) If a plaintiff who has once dismissed a civil action in any court commences a civil action based upon or including the same claim against the same defendant, the court may make an order for the payment of any unpaid costs of the civil action previously dismissed. In addition, if the plaintiff dismissed the previous civil action without prejudice within ten days of the date set for trial, the court may make an order for the payment of witness and other expenses, not including attorney fees, incurred by any other party that are caused to be incurred for the second trial because of the dismissal without prejudice of the previous civil action.
The court may stay the proceedings in the civil action until the plaintiff has complied with any such order.

correspondences.note_en: Article 384 provides for incidental termination of the proceeding through settlement, acquiescence, withdrawal of the claim, or death in non-transmissible actions, recorded by a decision divesting the court. correspondences.note_fr: L’article 385 énumère les causes d’extinction principale de l’instance—péremption, désistement d’instance et caducité de la citation—et préserve la possibilité d’une nouvelle instance si l’action subsiste. correspondences.note_fr: Le demandeur peut se désister de sa demande, en toute matière, afin de mettre fin à l’instance. Le Missouri autorise également le désistement volontaire, mais le droit de le faire sans ordonnance judiciaire est limité à certains stades de la procédure.
correspondences.note_en: The plaintiff may withdraw the claim in any matter to terminate the action. Missouri likewise permits voluntary dismissal, but the right to dismiss without a court order is limited to specified procedural stages.

correspondences.note_fr: Le désistement est en principe subordonné à l’acceptation du défendeur, sauf absence de défense au fond ou de fin de non-recevoir. correspondences.note_en: Withdrawal generally requires the defendant’s acceptance, unless the defendant has asserted no defense on the merits or objection to admissibility. Missouri regulates voluntary dismissal and requires an opposing-party stipulation in limited circumstances, but has no equivalent general acceptance requirement.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge doit déclarer le désistement parfait lorsque le refus du défendeur n’est pas fondé sur un motif légitime. Au Missouri, lorsque le désistement n’est pas un droit unilatéral, il nécessite une ordonnance judiciaire, mais le texte ne prévoit pas le critère du motif légitime du refus.
correspondences.note_en: The judge must declare the withdrawal effective when the defendant’s refusal lacks a legitimate reason. In Missouri, a voluntary dismissal outside the unilateral-dismissal period requires a court order, but the supplied texts do not adopt the French standard concerning the legitimacy of the refusal.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article admet le désistement et son acceptation sous une forme expresse ou implicite. La Rule 67.02 régit le dismissal volontaire du demandeur, mais ne prévoit pas expressément l’acceptation expresse ou implicite.
correspondences.note_en: The article allows withdrawal and its acceptance to be express or implied. Rule 67.02 governs voluntary dismissal by the plaintiff, but does not expressly address express or implied acceptance.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge constate l’extinction de l’instance, sans préciser ici le mode d’extinction. Les Rules 67.02 et 67.03 organisent la cessation de l’action par dismissal, et la Rule 67.01 en précise les effets, mais selon une technique et des conditions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The judge records the termination of the proceedings without specifying the particular mode of termination. Rules 67.02 and 67.03 provide for termination through dismissal, and Rule 67.01 states its effects, but by a different mechanism and under different conditions.

norms.heading: Involuntary Dismissal – Effect Thereof

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 67 — Dismissal of Civil Actions

norms.text: A defendant may move for an involuntary dismissal of the civil action for lack of jurisdiction, for prematurity of action, for failure to substitute a party for a decedent and for such other dismissals as are allowed by these Rules 41 through 101. Defendant may also move for an involuntary dismissal of the civil action for failure of the plaintiff to prosecute or to comply with these Rules 41 through 101 or any order of the court. Any involuntary dismissal shall be without prejudice unless the court in its order for dismissal shall otherwise specify.
