source_ids.text_source: Perplexity search-index copy of the courts.mo.gov page (pplx_sdk.content.snippets)

correspondences.note_fr: Le CPC met à la charge des parties la conduite de l’instance et l’accomplissement des actes dans les formes et délais requis. La Rule 44.01 encadre les délais et actes de procédure, et la Rule 67.03 permet une dismissal pour défaut de prosecution ou de respect des règles ou ordonnances.
correspondences.note_en: The CPC places responsibility for conducting the action and performing procedural acts in the required form and time on the parties. Rule 44.01 addresses procedural time limits and acts, while Rule 67.03 permits dismissal for failure to prosecute or comply with rules or court orders.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article définit la fin de non-recevoir comme un moyen d’irrecevabilité sans examen au fond, notamment pour défaut de qualité, intérêt, prescription ou chose jugée. Les textes du Missouri couvrent certains de ces moyens, mais ne mentionnent pas le défaut d’intérêt dans une catégorie générale identique.
correspondences.note_en: The article defines a procedural bar producing inadmissibility without reaching the merits, including lack of capacity, interest, limitations, and res judicata. The Missouri texts cover some of these matters but do not mention lack of interest in an identical general category.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article maintient la saisine du juge malgré l’interruption, autorise les mesures destinées à provoquer la reprise et permet la radiation en cas d’inaction. La Rule 67.03 permet un rejet pour défaut de diligence ou de respect d’une ordonnance, mais sur demande du défendeur et selon un effet distinct.
correspondences.note_en: The article preserves the judge’s jurisdiction after interruption, permits efforts to prompt resumption, and allows striking the case for inaction. Rule 67.03 permits dismissal for failure to prosecute or comply with an order, but generally on the defendant’s motion and with a different procedural effect.

correspondences.note_fr: La radiation sanctionne le défaut de diligence, retire l'affaire du rôle et impose une notification précisant le manquement. La Rule 84.08 prévoit une inscription au rôle des affaires à rejeter et une notification avec délai de régularisation en appel; la Rule 67.03 permet le rejet pour défaut de poursuivre l'action, mais non la radiation administrative.
correspondences.note_en: Radiation sanctions a failure to act, removes the case from the pending docket, and requires notice identifying the default. Rule 84.08 provides a dismissal docket and notice with an opportunity to cure in appeals; Rule 67.03 permits dismissal for failure to prosecute, but neither establishes the French administrative-radiation mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 385 énumère les causes d’extinction principale de l’instance—péremption, désistement d’instance et caducité de la citation—et préserve la possibilité d’une nouvelle instance si l’action subsiste. Les Rules 67.01 à 67.03 organisent les dismissals, notamment sans préjudice et avec possibilité de réintroduire l’action, mais ne couvrent pas exactement toutes les causes françaises ni le dessaisissement correspondant.
correspondences.note_en: Article 385 lists principal grounds for terminating a proceeding—lapse, withdrawal of the proceeding, and nullity or expiration of the summons—while preserving a new action if the claim survives. Rules 67.01–67.03 provide dismissals, often without prejudice and allowing refiling, but do not match all French grounds or the corresponding divestiture mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’instance est périmée après deux ans sans diligence d’aucune partie. La Rule 67.03 permet le rejet pour défaut de poursuivre l’action, mais sans délai fixe de deux ans et en principe sans préjudice ; la Rule 84.08 vise un défaut procédural en appel et le RSMo 514.170 règle surtout les frais.
correspondences.note_en: The action lapses after two years without any party taking procedural steps. Rule 67.03 permits dismissal for failure to prosecute, but sets no two-year period and generally makes dismissal without prejudice; Rule 84.08 concerns appellate default, while RSMo 514.170 primarily addresses costs.

correspondences.note_fr: La péremption peut être demandée par toute partie ou opposée après un acte tardif. La Rule 67.03 autorise le défendeur à demander le rejet pour défaut de poursuivre ; la Rule 84.08 prévoit, en appel, une mise en demeure suivie d’un rejet en cas de défaut non régularisé, sans mécanisme équivalent d’exception.
correspondences.note_en: Any party may seek dismissal for lapse, or raise it by exception after a late act. Rule 67.03 allows a defendant to move for dismissal for failure to prosecute; Rule 84.08 provides notice and dismissal for an unremedied appellate default, but neither supplies the same exception mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: La péremption éteint l’instance sans éteindre l’action et interdit de se prévaloir des actes de l’instance périmée. Les règles du Missouri organisent des dismissals, notamment pour défaut de poursuite, dont l’effet peut être sans préjudice, mais sans reprendre exactement cette règle sur les actes antérieurs.
correspondences.note_en: Lapse terminates the proceeding without extinguishing the claim and prevents reliance on acts in the lapsed proceeding. Missouri rules provide dismissals, including for failure to prosecute, which may be without prejudice, but do not reproduce the specific rule concerning prior procedural acts.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 468 prévoit les effets de la non-comparution injustifiée du demandeur : jugement au fond, renvoi, caducité de la citation et relevé de caducité sous quinze jours. La Rule 67.03 permet le rejet pour défaut de poursuite ou de respect des règles, la Rule 74.05 le jugement par défaut, et la Rule 65.01 le renvoi, mais aucune ne reprend l’ensemble de ce régime.
correspondences.note_en: Article 468 addresses the plaintiff’s unjustified failure to appear, allowing a merits judgment, continuance, dismissal for lapse of the summons, and reinstatement within fifteen days. Rule 67.03 permits dismissal for failure to prosecute or comply, Rule 74.05 permits default judgment, and Rule 65.01 permits continuances, but none reproduces the full regime.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 469 permet au juge de statuer au vu des éléments disponibles lorsqu’une partie ayant comparu n’accomplit plus les actes requis, et permet au défendeur de demander la caducité de la citation. La Rule 67.03 prévoit seulement le rejet pour défaut de poursuite ou de respect des règles.
correspondences.note_en: Article 469 permits judgment on the available materials when a party who appeared later fails to perform required procedural acts, and allows the defendant to seek lapse of the summons. Rule 67.03 provides only for dismissal for failure to prosecute or comply.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 470 permet au juge de radier d’office l’affaire lorsque toutes les parties n’accomplissent pas les actes requis dans les délais, après un dernier avis, par une décision insusceptible de recours. La Rule 67.03 vise également le défaut de poursuite ou de respect des règles, mais exige une demande du défendeur et prévoit en principe une radiation sans préjudice.
correspondences.note_en: Article 470 allows the judge, on his or her own initiative, to strike the case when no party takes the required procedural steps within the deadlines, after a final notice, by an unappealable decision. Rule 67.03 also addresses failure to prosecute or comply with procedural rules, but requires a defendant’s motion and generally makes the dismissal without prejudice.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 499-1 permet d’accorder une provision pour le procès et de rejeter rapidement une demande manifestement infondée. La Rule 74.04 organise le summary judgment et les textes relatifs au rejet permettent certaines sorties anticipées, mais aucun ne prévoit ces pouvoirs spécifiques pour la participation au débat public.
correspondences.note_en: Article 499-1 permits a litigation advance and rapid dismissal of a manifestly unfounded claim. Rule 74.04 provides summary judgment, while the dismissal provisions allow some early dispositions, but none establishes these specific powers for public-debate participation.

frcp.evidence: Committee Note – 1959 This rule is the same as Rule 56 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge constate l’extinction de l’instance, sans préciser ici le mode d’extinction. Les Rules 67.02 et 67.03 organisent la cessation de l’action par dismissal, et la Rule 67.01 en précise les effets, mais selon une technique et des conditions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The judge records the termination of the proceedings without specifying the particular mode of termination. Rules 67.02 and 67.03 provide for termination through dismissal, and Rule 67.01 states its effects, but by a different mechanism and under different conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article attribue au juge de la mise en état une compétence exclusive sur les exceptions, incidents, mesures provisoires et mesures d'instruction, ainsi que sur les fins de non-recevoir. Rule 55.27 et Rule 67.03 couvrent certaines contestations et décisions préalables, tandis que Rule 62.01 traite de la gestion préalable, sans équivalent global à cette compétence exclusive.
correspondences.note_en: This article gives the case-management judge exclusive authority over defenses, terminating incidents, provisional and evidentiary measures, and objections to admissibility. Rule 55.27 and Rule 67.03 cover some pretrial defenses and dismissals, while Rule 62.01 concerns case management; none reproduces the overall exclusive jurisdiction.

correspondences.note_fr: Le tribunal statue sur la demande, les demandes incidentes et les défenses au fond, et renvoie l'affaire en cas d'incompétence. La Rule 55.27 et le RSMo 509.400 organisent les défenses, notamment l'exception de compétence, tandis que la Rule 67.03 prévoit le rejet pour défaut de compétence, sans règle équivalente de renvoi.
correspondences.note_en: The court decides the claim, incidental claims, and defenses, and remands the case when it lacks jurisdiction. Rule 55.27 and RSMo 509.400 govern defenses, including jurisdictional objections, while Rule 67.03 provides dismissal for lack of jurisdiction rather than an equivalent remand mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit l’extinction de l’instance en cas de non-comparution ou de défaut de constitution d’avocat et rend non avenue l’ordonnance. Les textes du Missouri permettent le rejet et en précisent les effets, mais ne prévoient pas cette extinction ni l’anéantissement de l’ordonnance.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides for termination when the parties fail to appear or the creditor fails to obtain counsel, and renders the payment order ineffective. Missouri provisions allow dismissal and specify its effects, but do not provide for this specific termination or nullification of the order.

Rule 67.05 prévoit que les questions accessoires pendantes restent devant le tribunal après le désistement ou le rejet de l’action, mais ne pose pas une règle générale sur tous les incidents d’instance.
correspondences.note_en: Article 50 assigns procedural incidents to the court handling the affected proceeding. Rule 67.05 keeps pending ancillary matters before that court after dismissal, but does not establish a general rule governing all procedural incidents.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 126 prévoit la régularisation d’un vice avant que le juge statue, notamment par l’entrée en instance de la personne ayant qualité pour agir. Les textes du Missouri permettent la modification d’un acte, l’intervention ou la modification après une demande de rejet, sans reprendre cette règle générale.
correspondences.note_en: Article 126 permits cure of a defect before the court decides, including by the proper party joining the action. The Missouri texts allow amendment, intervention, or amendment after a dismissal motion, but do not reproduce the CPC’s general cure rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1385 prévoit un rejet définitif sans recours en cas de demande manifestement infondée ou irrecevable, ou de défaut de régularisation du formulaire, avec possibilité d’agir selon le droit commun. La Rule 67.06 prévoit le rejet après défaut d’amendement, tandis que la Rule 55.27 traite certains motifs de rejet et la Rule 81.01 renvoie au droit applicable pour l’appel, sans consacrer la même règle d’irrecevabilité du recours.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1385 makes dismissal unappealable in specified circumstances, including failure to correct the claim form, while preserving ordinary-law proceedings. Rule 67.06 addresses dismissal after failure to amend, Rule 55.27 covers certain dismissal grounds, and Rule 81.01 leaves appeal rights to law; none reproduces the same combined rule.

norms.heading: Masters in Circuit Courts

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 68 — Masters and Receivers

norms.text:
(a) Appointment and Compensation. Each circuit court in which any action is pending may appoint a master therein. The compensation to be allowed a master shall be charged upon such of the parties, or paid out of any fund or subject matter of the action which is in the custody or control of the court, as the court may direct.
(b) Reference. A reference to a master shall be the exception and not the rule. In actions to be tried by a jury, a reference shall be made only when the issues are complicated; in actions to be tried without a jury, save in matters of account and of difficult computation of damages, a reference shall be made only upon a showing that some exceptional condition requires it.
(c) Qualifications of Master. No person shall be appointed a master who is of kin to either party or is interested in the outcome of the action.

(d) Oath of Master. Before proceeding to hear any testimony in the action, a master shall take and subscribe an oath, before some officer duly authorized to administer an oath, faithfully to hear and examine the matters at issue and to make a just, impartial and true report.
(e) Powers. The order of reference to the master may specify or limit the master's powers and may direct the master to report only upon particular issues or to do or perform particular acts or to receive and report evidence only and may fix the time and place for beginning and closing the hearings and for the filing of the master's report.
Subject to the specifications and limitations stated in the order, the master has and shall exercise the power to regulate all proceedings in every hearing before the master and to do all acts and take all measures necessary or proper for the efficient performance of the duties under the order. The master may require the production of evidence upon all matters embraced in the reference.
The master may rule upon the admissibility of evidence unless otherwise directed by the order of reference and has the authority to put witnesses on oath and may examine them and may call the parties to the action and examine them upon oath. When a party so requests, the master shall make a record of the evidence offered and excluded in the same manner and subject to the same limitations as provided in Rule 73.01(a) for a court sitting without a jury.
(f) Proceedings.
(1) Meetings. When a reference is made, the clerk shall forthwith furnish the master with a copy of the order of reference. Upon receipt thereof, unless the order of reference otherwise provides, the master shall forthwith set a time and place for the first meeting of the parties, or their attorneys, to be held within thirty days after the date of the order of reference and shall notify the parties, or their attorneys.
It is the duty of the master to proceed with all reasonable diligence. Any party, on notice to the parties and master, may apply to the court for an order requiring the master to speed the proceedings and to make a report. If a party fails to appear at the time and place appointed, the master may proceed or, in the master's discretion, adjourn the proceedings to a future day, giving notice thereof to the absent party.
(2) Witnesses. The parties may procure the attendance of witnesses before the master by the issuance and service of subpoenas issued by the clerk of the appointing court. The failure of any person to comply with the requirements of any subpoena issued as herein provided shall be reported promptly to the court issuing the subpoena. Witnesses shall receive the same fees as would be allowed them as witnesses in a civil case in circuit court.
Sheriff and all other officers shall be entitled to the same fees for services performed in references to a master, as would be allowed them in their respective courts for similar services. All costs incurred in a reference shall be taxed in the pending case in circuit court.
(3) Statement of Accounts. When matters of accounting are in issue before the master, the master may prescribe the form in which the accounts shall be submitted and in any proper case may require or receive in evidence a statement by a certified public accountant who is called as a witness. Upon objection of a party to any of the items thus submitted or upon a showing that the form of statement is insufficient, the master may require a different form of statement to be furnished, or the accounts or specific items thereof to be proved by oral examination of the accounting parties or upon written interrogatories or in such other manner as the master directs.
(4) Depositions. Depositions of witnesses or parties taken in the action may be read in evidence before the master as in cases of trials before the court.

(g) Report.

(1) Contents and Filing. The master shall prepare a report upon the matters submitted by the order of reference and if required to make findings of fact and conclusions of law shall set them forth in the report. The master shall file the report with the clerk of the court together with a transcript of the proceedings including the evidence and exhibits, if any. The clerk shall forthwith mail to all parties notice of the filing and a copy of the master's report.
(2) Objections. Any party within thirty days after being served with notice of the filing of the master's report may file written objections thereto and serve them upon the other parties.
(3) Action on Report and Use in Jury Trials. If no objections are filed, the court may adopt the report. If objections are filed, or the court proposes action other than adoption of the report, the court, after hearing, may adopt the report or may modify it or may reject it in whole or in part or may receive further evidence or may recommit it with instructions.
If issues are to be tried by a jury, the master's findings on the issues submitted to the master may be reported to the jury as having been determined and only fact issues other than those determined by the master shall be submitted to or determined by the jury.

(4) Stipulation as to Findings. If the parties stipulate that a master's findings of fact shall be final and binding upon them, only questions of law arising upon the master's report shall thereafter be considered.
(5) Draft Report. Before filing the report a master may submit a draft thereof to counsel for all parties for the purpose of receiving their suggestions.

(h) Masters for Depositions. The court, upon motion, may appoint a master to preside at the taking of a deposition. The master shall be a member of The Missouri Bar.
The master, in addition to the authority conferred on officers to take depositions, shall have the authority to determine all objections to evidence and to exclude evidence that is not within the scope of discovery as defined in Rule 56.01(b).
Upon request of a party, the master shall report a ruling or rulings on evidence to the court either during or after the completion of the taking of a deposition. Within 30 days after being served with a copy of the master's report, any party may file written objections thereto and serve them on the other parties. If objections are filed, the court shall issue an order sustaining or overruling the objections.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article prévoit que le technicien joigne au rapport les observations ou réclamations écrites des parties et indique les suites qui leur sont données. La Rule 68.01 prévoit la communication du rapport du master et les objections écrites; RSMo 515.170 et 515.200 organisent aussi la consignation et la présentation des exceptions, mais dans le cadre judiciaire des referees.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires the technician to attach the parties’ written observations or objections to the report and state how they were addressed. Rule 68.01 provides service and written objections to a master’s report, while RSMo 515.170 and 515.200 address written exceptions in referee proceedings, but none has the same private-technician procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article impose la remise d'un rapport écrit aux parties et attribue, dans une convention entre avocats, une valeur équivalente à celle d'un avis d'expert judiciaire. La Rule 60.01(b) prévoit la remise de rapports d'examen, y compris pour les examens convenus, et la Rule 68.01 ainsi que RSMo 452.390 organisent la remise de rapports, mais aucun ne confère exactement cette valeur probatoire à un rapport privé de technicien.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires a written report to be delivered to the parties and gives a report under an agreement between lawyers the same value as a court-appointed expert opinion. Rule 60.01(b) covers reports, including agreed examinations, and Rule 68.01 and RSMo 452.390 govern report disclosure, but none gives precisely the same evidentiary status to a privately retained technician’s report.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut réentendre les témoins, les confronter entre eux ou avec les parties, éventuellement en présence d’un technicien. La Rule 57.03 permet, sous conditions, une nouvelle déposition ; la Rule 68.01 permet au master de conduire une audition et d’examiner les témoins, sans prévoir expressément la confrontation ni l’assistance d’un technicien.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may hear witnesses again, confront them with one another or with the parties, and, where appropriate, conduct the hearing with a technician present. Rule 57.03 permits a further deposition subject to conditions, and Rule 68.01 permits a master to conduct hearings and examine witnesses, but neither expressly provides for confrontation or a technician.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet au juge d’autoriser le témoin à percevoir les indemnités auxquelles il a droit. Rule 68.01 prévoit les frais dus aux témoins devant un master, et RSMo 454.1584 permet, dans les procédures alimentaires, le remboursement des frais raisonnables des témoins; ces règles ont un champ ou une structure différents.
correspondences.note_en: The article allows the judge to authorize a witness to receive applicable compensation. Rule 68.01 provides witness fees in proceedings before a master, while RSMo 454.1584 permits recovery of reasonable witness expenses in support proceedings; both differ in scope or structure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article français impose que la décision fixe le jour, l’heure et le lieu de l’enquête devant le juge. La Rule 68.01 permet à l’ordre de référence de fixer le calendrier et le lieu des audiences devant un master, mais dans un cadre institutionnel différent.
correspondences.note_en: The French article requires the order to set the date, time, and place of the inquiry before the judge. Rule 68.01 permits the reference order to set the timing and place of hearings before a master, but in a different institutional framework.

correspondences.note_fr: La Rule 68.01 autorise le tribunal à désigner un master, dont l’ordonnance peut définir les actes à accomplir et qui doit établir un rapport. Elle ne reprend pas expressément les trois modalités de l’article 232; les dispositions relatives aux enquêtes de garde ne sont pas retenues.
correspondences.note_en: Rule 68.01 authorizes appointment of a master whose order may define the acts to be performed and who must prepare a report. It does not expressly reproduce all three methods in article 232; the custody-investigation provision is not retained.

correspondences.note_fr: Les techniciens peuvent être récusés pour les mêmes causes que les juges, avec une déclaration et une contestation selon un calendrier précis. Les règles et textes du Missouri imposent surtout que le master ou le referee soit désintéressé et exempt de motifs d’exception, sans prévoir l’ensemble des causes, délais et déclarations de l’article 234.
correspondences.note_en: Technicians may be challenged on the same grounds as judges, with specified timing and self-disclosure requirements. The Missouri provisions chiefly require masters or referees to be disinterested and free from exceptions, but do not reproduce the article’s full grounds, timing, or self-reporting procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge français n’est pas lié par les constatations ou conclusions du technicien. La Rule 68.01 permet au tribunal d’adopter, modifier ou rejeter tout ou partie du rapport du master, mais certaines conclusions peuvent devenir contraignantes en cas de stipulation des parties.
correspondences.note_en: The French judge is not bound by the technician’s findings or conclusions. Rule 68.01 permits the court to adopt, modify, or reject a master’s report in whole or in part, although the parties may stipulate that the master’s findings are final and binding.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 248 interdit au technicien de recevoir directement d’une partie toute rémunération ou remboursement de débours, sauf décision du juge. Les Rules 68.01 et 68.03 prévoient que la rémunération du master est fixée ou répartie par le tribunal, et le RSMo 515.220 soumet celle du referee à l’autorisation du tribunal, sans reprendre expressément l’interdiction de paiement direct.
correspondences.note_en: Article 248 bars a court-appointed technician from receiving remuneration or reimbursement directly from a party unless authorized by the judge. Rules 68.01 and 68.03 provide that a master’s compensation is directed by the court, and RSMo 515.220 makes a referee’s compensation court-allowed, but none expressly states the direct-payment prohibition.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge fixe le délai du rapport ou la date de présentation et désigne les parties qui verseront une provision, dont il fixe le montant. La Rule 68.01 permet de fixer le délai du rapport et de mettre la rémunération du master à la charge de certaines parties, sans prévoir expressément cette avance provisionnelle ni son montant.
correspondences.note_en: The judge sets the report deadline or presentation date and identifies the parties that must advance the technician’s compensation. Rule 68.01 permits setting the master’s reporting time and charging compensation to designated parties, but does not expressly provide for an advance payment or its amount.

correspondences.note_fr: Le constat est déposé au greffe, les constatations orales sont consignées et les pièces justificatives sont jointes au dossier. La Rule 68.01(g)(1) impose au master le dépôt d’un rapport avec la transcription, les preuves et les pièces ; le RSMo 515.190 impose également le retour du rapport et des témoignages au tribunal.
correspondences.note_en: The report is filed with the clerk, oral observations are recorded, and supporting documents are attached to the case file. Rule 68.01(g)(1) requires a master to file a report with the proceeding transcript, evidence, and exhibits; RSMo 515.190 likewise requires the report and testimony to be returned to the court.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 255 prévoit que le juge fixe la rémunération du constatant après justification de l’accomplissement de sa mission et peut lui délivrer un titre exécutoire. La Rule 68.01(a) règle la rémunération d’un master nommé par le tribunal, tandis que le RSMo 515.220 concerne celle des referees ; aucun des deux textes ne prévoit le titre exécutoire ni la condition d’achèvement de la mission.
correspondences.note_en: Article 255 provides that the judge fixes the court-appointed investigator’s compensation after proof that the assignment was completed and may issue an enforceable title. Rule 68.01(a) addresses compensation of a court-appointed master, and RSMo 515.220 addresses referees’ compensation; neither provides for an enforceable title or the completion-based condition.

correspondences.note_fr: La consultation peut être ordonnée à tout moment et est normalement orale, sauf ordre de consignation écrite. La Rule 68.01 organise les réunions et le dépôt du rapport d’un master, mais ne reprend pas cette faculté générale ni l’alternative entre présentation orale et écrite.
correspondences.note_en: A consultation may be ordered at any time and is ordinarily presented orally unless the court requires a written record. Rule 68.01 governs a master’s proceedings and report, but does not provide the same general timing rule or oral-versus-written alternative.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge fixe la date de présentation ou le délai de dépôt et désigne les parties tenues de verser une avance dont il fixe le montant. La Rule 68.01 permet de fixer le calendrier des audiences et du rapport et d’imputer la rémunération aux parties; les articles 515.220 et 515.090 concernent respectivement la rémunération et la fixation de l’audience, sans prévoir cette avance.
correspondences.note_en: The judge sets the presentation date or filing deadline and identifies the parties responsible for an advance payment in an amount fixed by the court. Rule 68.01 addresses scheduling hearings and the report and allocating compensation; RSMo 515.220 and 515.090 address compensation and hearing arrangements, but not this advance-payment mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 262 prévoit que le juge fixe la rémunération du consultant après justification de l’accomplissement de sa mission et peut lui délivrer un titre exécutoire. La Rule 68.01(a) et le RSMo 515.220 organisent la rémunération de personnes désignées comme master ou referee, mais ne prévoient pas la délivrance d’un titre exécutoire et imposent des cadres différents.
correspondences.note_en: Article 262 lets the judge set a consultant’s compensation after the mission is performed and permits issuance of an enforceable title. Rule 68.01(a) and RSMo 515.220 address compensation for court-appointed masters or referees, but do not provide for an enforceable title and operate under materially different institutional rules.

correspondences.note_fr: RSMo 210.842, limité aux procédures de protection de l’enfance, permet d’imputer par jugement les frais raisonnables d’experts selon les proportions et échéances fixées par le tribunal. La Rule 68.01(a) répartit la rémunération d’un master, mais aucune de ces dispositions ne prévoit la consignation préalable d’une provision d’expertise.
correspondences.note_en: RSMo 210.842, limited to child-protection proceedings, permits judgment for reasonable expert fees in proportions and at times set by the court. Rule 68.01(a) allocates a master’s compensation, but neither provision creates a French-style advance deposit for expert fees.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 282 règle la forme et le dépôt de l’avis d’expert, les divergences entre experts, les avis de techniciens auxiliaires et la demande de rémunération. La Rule 68.01(g) prévoit le dépôt, la notification et les objections au rapport du master, tandis que le paragraphe (a) traite de sa rémunération, mais l’institution et les modalités diffèrent.
correspondences.note_en: Article 282 governs the form and filing of an expert opinion, differing experts, auxiliary technical opinions, and the expert’s compensation request. Rule 68.01(g) addresses filing, notice, and objections to a master’s report, and subsection (a) addresses compensation, but the institution and procedures differ.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 284 organise la fixation et le paiement de la rémunération de l’expert, ainsi que les observations sur son montant et le titre exécutoire. La Rule 68.01(a) règle la rémunération du master et sa charge entre les parties, mais ne prévoit pas l’ensemble de ces garanties et modalités.
correspondences.note_en: Article 284 governs fixing and paying the expert’s compensation, comments on the amount, and issuance of an enforceable title. Rule 68.01(a) addresses a master’s compensation and allocation among the parties, but does not contain all of these safeguards and procedures.

correspondences.note_fr: Le texte français permet au juge de désigner un tiers, de définir sa mission et le délai du rapport, et exige une compétence professionnelle dans le domaine. La Rule 68.01 prévoit la désignation d’un master ainsi que la définition de ses pouvoirs et du délai de son rapport; le RSMo 515.030 prévoit la nomination de referees aptes, sans exiger une compétence professionnelle déterminée.
correspondences.note_en: The French text permits the court to appoint a third party, define the assignment and reporting deadline, and requires professional competence in the relevant field. Rule 68.01 provides for appointing a master and defining the master’s powers and reporting deadline; RSMo 515.030 provides for appointing suitable referees without requiring a specified professional competence.

correspondences.note_fr: Le greffe notifie la décision au tiers, recueille son acceptation et subordonne en principe le début de la mission au versement d’une provision. La Rule 68.01 prévoit la transmission immédiate de l’ordre par le greffe et le commencement des opérations, mais ni l’acceptation ni une provision; le RSMo 515.100 concerne seulement la signification des avis.
correspondences.note_en: The clerk notifies the appointee, obtains acceptance, and generally conditions commencement on payment of an advance. Rule 68.01 provides prompt delivery of the reference order and commencement of proceedings, but not acceptance or an advance; RSMo 515.100 concerns service of notices only.

correspondences.note_fr: Le coût de la mission incombe à l’auteur du manquement; le juge fixe une provision proche de la rémunération prévisible et le délai de consignation, avec échéances éventuelles. La Rule 68.01 règle l’imputation de la rémunération, la Rule 77.02 la garantie des frais anticipés, et le RSMo 515.220 la rémunération des referees, sans reprendre ce mécanisme complet.
correspondences.note_en: The violator bears the mission cost, while the court fixes an advance approximating expected compensation and a deposit deadline, with possible installments. Rule 68.01 addresses allocation of a master’s compensation, Rule 77.02 security for anticipated costs, and RSMo 515.220 referee compensation, but none reproduces the full mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise le signalement des difficultés d’un tiers chargé d’une mission et la prorogation judiciaire du délai de rapport. La Rule 68.01 encadre la mission, la diligence et le rapport du master; les sections 515.060 et 515.190 imposent également diligence et célérité, sans prévoir expressément cette procédure de prorogation.
correspondences.note_en: The article addresses difficulties encountered by an appointed third party and judicial extension of the reporting deadline. Rule 68.01 governs a master’s assignment, diligence, and report; sections 515.060 and 515.190 likewise require diligence and prompt reporting, but do not expressly provide this extension procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article règle l’acompte, la provision complémentaire et la conséquence du défaut de consignation pour un tiers chargé d’un rapport. La Rule 68.01 traite de la rémunération du master et de son imputation, la Rule 77.02 de la garantie des frais anticipés et la section 515.220 de la rémunération des arbitres, mais aucune ne reprend l’ensemble de ce mécanisme.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs an advance payment, supplemental security, and the consequence of failing to deposit it for a reporting third party. Rule 68.01 addresses a master’s compensation and its allocation, Rule 77.02 anticipated-cost security, and section 515.220 referee compensation, but none reproduces the complete mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: Le tiers remet son rapport, transmet sa demande de rémunération aux parties et permet à l’auteur du manquement de présenter des observations dans les quinze jours. La Rule 68.01 prévoit le dépôt et la notification du rapport du master, tandis que les autres textes concernent la rémunération et les demandes de frais, sans reprendre exactement cette procédure.
correspondences.note_en: The third party files a report, serves the parties with a fee request, and allows the alleged violator fifteen days to comment. Rule 68.01 addresses filing and service of a master’s report, while the other provisions address compensation or fee applications without reproducing this exact procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge fixe la rémunération selon le travail accompli, règle les sommes consignées ou leur restitution, recueille les observations en cas de réduction et délivre un titre exécutoire. Les textes du Missouri permettent au tribunal de fixer ou d’allouer une rémunération et de taxer certains frais, mais ne prévoient pas l’ensemble de ces mécanismes.
correspondences.note_en: The court fixes compensation based on the work performed, applies or refunds deposited sums, invites comments before reducing the requested amount, and issues an enforceable title. The Missouri provisions allow court-set compensation or taxation of certain fees, but do not provide all of these mechanisms.

correspondences.note_fr: La rémunération du distributeur est prélevée sur les fonds et supportée au prorata par les créanciers, avec fixation judiciaire en cas de contestation. La Rule 96.30 concerne les honoraires, frais et indemnités en matière de partage, et la Rule 68.01 permet d’imputer la rémunération d’un master aux parties ou au fonds selon les directives du tribunal, sans règle de prorata.
correspondences.note_en: The distributor’s compensation is deducted from the fund and borne pro rata by the creditors, with judicial fixation if disputed. Rule 96.30 addresses fees, costs, and compensation in partition proceedings, and Rule 68.01 permits a master’s compensation to be charged to parties or the fund as the court directs, but neither provides the article’s pro-rata rule.

correspondences.note_fr: Le notaire convoque les parties, recueille les documents, signale les difficultés au juge et peut demander des mesures ou l’assistance d’un expert. Rule 68.01 confère au master des pouvoirs de convocation, de conduite et de production de preuves, tandis que RSMo 515.130 vise spécifiquement la production de documents, sans reprendre l’ensemble du mécanisme ni l’adjonction d’un expert.
correspondences.note_en: The notary convenes the parties, obtains documents, reports difficulties to the judge, and may seek measures or expert assistance. Rule 68.01 gives a master comparable procedural and evidence-gathering powers, and RSMo 515.130 addresses document production, but neither reproduces the full mechanism or expert-assistance provision.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit une conciliation devant le juge puis un procès-verbal et un projet d’état liquidatif par le notaire. Les textes Missouri retenus concernent seulement la conduite et le rapport d’un master ou de referees; ils ne prévoient ni cette conciliation ni ce projet.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides for court-assisted conciliation followed by minutes and a draft liquidation statement prepared by the notary. The retained Missouri texts concern only proceedings and reporting by a master or referees; they provide neither the conciliation nor the liquidation draft.

norms.heading: Receivers in Circuit Courts

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 68 — Masters and Receivers

norms.text:
(a) Appointment of Receiver. Whenever in a pending legal or equitable proceeding it appears to the court that a receiver is necessary to keep, preserve and protect any business, business interest or property, including money or other thing deposited in court or the subject of a tender, the court, or any judge thereof in vacation, may appoint a receiver whose duty it shall be to keep, preserve and protect, to the extent and in the manner that the court may direct, that which the receiver is ordered to take into the receiver's charge.
(b) Bond of Receiver. Such receiver shall give bond, and have the same powers and be subject to all the provisions, as far as they may be applicable, enjoined upon a receiver appointed by virtue of the law providing for suits by attachment.

(c) Compensation of Receiver. The court shall allow the receiver reasonable compensation for his services to be charged upon such of the parties, or paid out of any fund or subject matter of the action which is in the custody or control of the court, as the court may direct.

Paragraph (b) is the same as prior Rule 68.25.

The sources of paragraph (C) are Rule 53 (a) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure and prior Rule 68.26.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 873 vise les mesures conservatoires ou de remise en état en cas de dommage imminent ou de trouble manifestement illicite, ainsi que la provision lorsque l’obligation n’est pas sérieusement contestable. La Rule 92.02 couvre principalement les mesures injonctives d’urgence ; la Rule 68.02 permet la préservation de biens par un receiver, sans prévoir la provision française.
correspondences.note_en: Article 873 covers protective or restorative measures for imminent harm or manifestly unlawful interference, and provisional payment or performance when the obligation is not seriously disputed. Rule 92.02 chiefly addresses emergency injunctive relief; Rule 68.02 permits preservation of property through a receiver, but does not provide the French-style provisional award.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1537 confirme que la mise en œuvre d’une conciliation ou médiation conventionnelle n’empêche pas le juge d’ordonner une mesure d’instruction, provisoire ou conservatoire. Les règles du Missouri régissent certaines de ces mesures, mais ne prévoient pas expressément leur maintien ou leur ordonnance malgré une procédure amiable conventionnelle.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1537 provides that conventional conciliation or mediation does not prevent the court from ordering an investigative, provisional, or conservatory measure. The Missouri rules govern particular forms of such measures, but do not expressly address ordering them notwithstanding conventional ADR.

norms.heading: Masters in Appellate Courts

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 68 — Masters and Receivers

norms.text:
(a) Appointment and Compensation. Each appellate court in which any action is pending may appoint a master therein. The compensation to be allowed to a master shall be charged upon such of the parties, or paid out of any fund or subject matter of the action which is in the custody and control of the court, as the court may direct.

(b) Qualifications of Master. No person shall be appointed a master who is of kin to either party or is interested in the outcome of the action.

(c) Oath of Master. Before proceeding to hear any testimony in the action, a master shall take and subscribe an oath, before some officer duly authorized to administer an oath, faithfully to hear and examine the matters at issue and to make a just, impartial and true report.

(d) Powers. The order of reference to the master may specify or limit the master's powers and may direct the master to report only upon particular issues or to do or perform particular acts or to receive and report evidence only and may fix the time and place for beginning and closing the hearings and for the filing of the master's report. Subject to the specifications and limitations stated in the order, the master has and shall exercise the power to regulate all proceedings in every hearing before the master and to do all acts and take all measures necessary or proper for the efficient performance of the duties under the order. The master may require the production of evidence upon all matters embraced in the reference. The master may rule upon the admissibility of evidence unless otherwise directed by the order of reference and has the authority to put witnesses on oath and may examine them and may call the parties to the action and examine them upon oath. When a party so requests, the master shall make a record of the evidence offered and excluded in the same manner and subject to the same limitations as provided in Rule 73.01(a) for a court sitting without a jury.

(e) Proceedings.

(1) Meetings. When a reference is made, the clerk shall forthwith furnish the master with a copy of the order of reference. Upon receipt thereof, unless the order of reference otherwise provides, the master shall forthwith set a time and place for the first meeting of the parties, or their attorneys, to be held within thirty days after the date of the order of reference and shall notify the parties, or their attorneys. It is the duty of the master to proceed with all reasonable diligence. Any party, on notice to the parties and master, may apply to the court for an order requiring the master to speed the proceedings and to make the report. If a party fails to appear at the time and place appointed, the master may proceed or, in the master's discretion, adjourn the proceedings to a future day, giving notice thereof to the absent party.

(2) Witnesses. The parties may procure the attendance of witnesses before the master by the issuance and service of subpoenas issued by the clerk of the appointing court. The failure of any person to comply with the requirements of any subpoena issued as herein provided shall be reported promptly to the court issuing the subpoena.

(f) Report. The master shall prepare a report upon the matters submitted by the order of reference and, if required to make findings of fact and conclusions of law, they shall be set forth in the report. The master shall file the report with the clerk of the court together with a transcript of the proceedings including the evidence and exhibits, if any. The clerk shall forthwith mail to all parties notice of the filing and a copy of the master's report.

(g) Exceptions. Any party may, but is not required to, file exceptions to the report to be ruled upon by the master. The master may amend findings of fact or make new findings of fact and conclusions of law. Exceptions shall not be permitted to any revised report by the master. The exceptions shall be filed not later than thirty days after the filing of the report by the master. If the exceptions are not passed on by the master within thirty days after filing, they are deemed denied for all purposes. The filing of exceptions with the master shall not preclude any party from alleging or asserting any point in the appellate court.

(h) Docketing. After there has been a ruling on exceptions to the report of the master, or if no exceptions are filed after the expiration of thirty days from the time the master's report was filed, the case shall be docketed for hearing in the appellate court.

correspondences.note_fr: Le technicien doit révéler, avant d’accepter, toute circonstance affectant son indépendance ou son impartialité. Les règles du Missouri exigent surtout que le referee ou le master soit désintéressé, tandis que Rule 88.06 impose une divulgation des relations et intérêts susceptibles de créer un biais au médiateur.
correspondences.note_en: Before accepting, the technician must disclose circumstances affecting independence or impartiality. Missouri mainly requires referees and masters to be disinterested, while Rule 88.06 expressly requires mediators to disclose relationships and interests that could create bias or conflicts.

correspondences.note_fr: Le technicien doit agir avec diligence et impartialité, respecter la contradiction, exécuter personnellement sa mission et s’abstenir de toute appréciation juridique. Le Missouri impose diligence, impartialité et serment aux referees ou masters, mais les textes fournis ne reprennent pas l’ensemble de ces obligations.
correspondences.note_en: The technician must act diligently and impartially, respect adversarial procedure, perform the mission personally, and avoid legal judgments. Missouri imposes diligence, impartiality, and an oath on referees or masters, but the supplied provisions do not reproduce all of these duties.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut ordonner une mesure d'instruction supplémentaire rendue utile par l'exécution de la première. La Rule 60.01 et le RSMo 452.390 permettent certaines mesures judiciaires d'examen ou d'enquête, tandis que la Rule 68.03(d) confère au master des pouvoirs accessoires nécessaires, mais dans un cadre plus limité.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may order an additional evidentiary measure made useful by carrying out the first. Rule 60.01 and RSMo 452.390 authorize specific court-ordered examinations or investigations, while Rule 68.03(d) gives a master ancillary powers, but under narrower conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: Les difficultés d'exécution sont réglées par le juge compétent, à la demande des parties, du technicien ou d'office. La Rule 61.01 prévoit des mesures judiciaires en cas de non-exécution d'une mesure de découverte, la Rule 60.01 organise l'exécution des examens, et la Rule 68.03(d) la conduite des opérations du master.
correspondences.note_en: Execution difficulties are resolved by the responsible judge on a party's, technician's, or the court's own initiative. Rule 61.01 provides judicial responses to failures in discovery, Rule 60.01 structures examinations, and Rule 68.03(d) regulates a master's proceedings.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge statue immédiatement pendant l'opération; sinon, il convoque les parties et le technicien à une date fixée par le greffe. La Rule 68.03(e)(1) prévoit une réunion et sa notification par le master, la Rule 60.01(a)(3) précise lieu et modalités, et la Rule 55.29 autorise les actes en chambre.
correspondences.note_en: The judge rules immediately during the operation; otherwise, the clerk summons the parties and technician to a scheduled hearing. Rule 68.03(e)(1) provides for a noticed meeting, Rule 60.01(a)(3) specifies examination details, and Rule 55.29 permits judicial acts in chambers.

correspondences.note_fr: Les techniciens peuvent être récusés pour les mêmes causes que les juges, avec une déclaration et une contestation selon un calendrier précis. Les règles et textes du Missouri imposent surtout que le master ou le referee soit désintéressé et exempt de motifs d’exception, sans prévoir l’ensemble des causes, délais et déclarations de l’article 234.
correspondences.note_en: Technicians may be challenged on the same grounds as judges, with specified timing and self-disclosure requirements. The Missouri provisions chiefly require masters or referees to be disinterested and free from exceptions, but do not reproduce the article’s full grounds, timing, or self-reporting procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 236 permet au juge d’accroître ou de restreindre la mission confiée au technicien. La Rule 68.03(d) permet à l’ordre de renvoi de préciser ou limiter les pouvoirs et questions confiés au master, sans reprendre expressément la modification ultérieure de la mission.
correspondences.note_en: Article 236 allows the judge to enlarge or restrict the technician’s assignment. Rule 68.03(d) allows the reference order to specify or limit a master’s powers and issues, but does not expressly address later modification of the assignment.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 237 impose au technicien d’exercer sa mission avec conscience, objectivité et impartialité. La Rule 68.03(c) et le RSMo 515.050 imposent un serment d’impartialité et de rapport juste, tandis que le RSMo 515.040 exclut les referees intéressés, sans formuler exactement une obligation générale de conduite.
correspondences.note_en: Article 237 requires the technician to perform the assignment conscientiously, objectively, and impartially. Rule 68.03(c) and RSMo 515.050 require an impartial oath and a just report, while RSMo 515.040 disqualifies interested referees, without stating the same general conduct duty.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 248 interdit au technicien de recevoir directement d’une partie toute rémunération ou remboursement de débours, sauf décision du juge. Les Rules 68.01 et 68.03 prévoient que la rémunération du master est fixée ou répartie par le tribunal, et le RSMo 515.220 soumet celle du referee à l’autorisation du tribunal, sans reprendre expressément l’interdiction de paiement direct.
correspondences.note_en: Article 248 bars a court-appointed technician from receiving remuneration or reimbursement directly from a party unless authorized by the judge. Rules 68.01 and 68.03 provide that a master’s compensation is directed by the court, and RSMo 515.220 makes a referee’s compensation court-allowed, but none expressly states the direct-payment prohibition.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet à une partie de déférer le serment et charge le juge d’en vérifier l’admissibilité et la pertinence des faits. La Rule 68.03 et les RSMo 210.832 et Rule 57.03 organisent respectivement l’examen sous serment, la contrainte de témoignage pertinent ou la déposition, mais sans reprendre le mécanisme général du serment décisoire.
correspondences.note_en: The article lets a party refer an oath and requires the judge to assess admissibility and select relevant facts. Rule 68.03, RSMo 210.832, and Rule 57.03 provide for sworn examination, compelled testimony on relevant facts, or depositions, but do not reproduce the general decisive-oath mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: Lorsque le serment est déféré d’office, le juge fixe les faits concernés. RSMo 210.832 permet au tribunal d’ordonner un témoignage sous serment sur les faits pertinents, tandis que la Rule 68.03 permet de limiter une référence à des questions déterminées, sans prévoir le serment judiciaire d’office.
correspondences.note_en: When the oath is administered ex officio, the judge determines the facts covered. RSMo 210.832 permits the court to compel sworn testimony concerning relevant facts, and Rule 68.03 permits a reference limited to particular issues, but neither provides the French ex officio judicial-oath procedure.

norms.text:
Upon the court's own motion or upon the request of any party, the court shall permit jurors to take notes. If jurors are permitted to take notes, the court shall supply each juror with suitable materials.

Jurors shall not take their notes out of the courtroom except to use their notes during deliberations.
The court shall collect all juror notes immediately before discharge of the jury.

After the jury is discharged, the court shall destroy the notes promptly without permitting their review by the court or any other person.

Juror notes shall not be used to impeach a verdict.

norms.heading: Juror Nondisclosure

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 69 — Trial by Jury

norms.text:
(a) Proposed Questions. A party seeking to inquire as to the litigation history of potential jurors shall make a record of the proposed initial questions before voir dire. Failure to follow this procedure shall result in waiver of the right to inquire as to litigation history.

(b) Reasonable Investigation. For purposes of this Rule 69.025, a "reasonable investigation" means review of Case.net before the jury is sworn.
(c) Opportunity to Investigate. The court shall give all parties an opportunity to conduct a reasonable investigation as to whether a prospective juror has been a party to litigation.

(d) Procedure When Nondisclosure is Suspected. A party who has reasonable grounds to believe that a prospective juror has failed to disclose that he or she has been a party to litigation must so inform the court before the jury is sworn. The court shall then question the prospective juror or jurors outside the presence of the other prospective jurors.
(e) Waiver. A party waives the right to seek relief based on juror nondisclosure of information that would be readily apparent from a reasonable investigation unless the party does the following before the jury is sworn:

(1) Conducts a reasonable investigation; and

(2) Informs the court of the basis for believing that such nondisclosure has occurred.
(f) Post-Trial Proceedings. A party seeking post-trial relief based on juror nondisclosure has the burden of demonstrating compliance with Rule 69.025(d) and Rule 69.025(e) may satisfy that burden by affidavit. The court shall then conduct an evidentiary hearing to determine if relief should be granted.

norms.heading: Instructions to Juries

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 70 — Instructions

norms.text:
(a) Requests for Instructions. Any party may, and a party with the burden of proof on an issue shall, submit written requests for instructions on the law applicable to the issues. Requests shall be submitted prior to an instruction conference or at such time as the court directs. A party need not request a converse instruction until the court has indicated the verdict directing instruction expected to be given.
The court may give instructions without requests of counsel. All instructions shall be submitted in writing and shall be given or refused by the court according to the law and the evidence in the case. Each instruction shall be submitted with an original and one copy for the court and one copy for each party. Each copy shall indicate whether it was prepared at the court's direction or by which party it was tendered and shall contain a notation as follows:
'MAI No. ___' or 'MAI No. ___ modified' or 'Not in MAI' as the case may be.
(b) Form of Instructions. Whenever Missouri Approved Instructions contains an instruction applicable in a particular case that the appropriate party requests or the court decides to submit, such instruction shall be given to the exclusion of any other instructions on the same subject. Where an MAI must be modified to fairly submit the issues in a particular case, or where there is no applicable MAI so that an instruction not in MAI must be given, then such modifications or such instructions shall be simple, brief, impartial, free from argument, and shall not submit to the jury or require findings of detailed evidentiary facts.
(c) Violation of Rule – Effect. The giving of an instruction in violation of the provisions of this Rule 70.02 shall constitute error, its prejudicial effect to be judicially determined, provided that objection has been timely made pursuant to Rule 70.03.

(d) Converse Instruction – Effect of Requesting. The request of a converse instruction shall not be deemed to waive any objection to the instruction conversed.
(e) Instructions Conference and Record. The court shall hold an instructions conference on the record with counsel to determine the instructions to be given. The court shall inform counsel as to the instructions that are to be given prior to the time they are delivered to the jury. All instructions refused and all instructions given, including a record of who tendered them, shall be kept as a part of a record in the case.
Counsel shall make specific objections on the record, out of the hearing of the jury, during the instructions conference. Prior to the instructions conference on the record, the court may conduct informal discussions with counsel regarding jury instructions. The court may correct clerical errors in instructions at any time prior to verdict.
(f) Instructions – How and When Given. After a jury has been sworn to try a case but before opening statements, the court shall read to the jury Missouri Approved Instructions 2.01, which shall be marked and given to the jury along with the other instructions at the close of the case but shall not be reread by the court.
The court may give such other preliminary instructions during the trial as will assist the jury in understanding its role or the issues in the case. Agreement is not required for cautionary or withdrawal instructions during the trial. Final instructions in the case, submitting the law applicable to the case, shall be given prior to final arguments. Instructions that are to be given shall be consecutively numbered and all shall be given as instructions of the court.
Except where otherwise provided in Missouri Approved Instructions, they shall be given in such order as the court shall deem advisable. The final instructions on the law governing the case shall be read to the jury by the court and provided to the jury in writing.

norms.heading: Verdict of Jury – General or Special

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 71 — Verdicts

norms.text:
The verdict of a jury is either general or special. A general verdict is one by which the jury pronounces generally upon all or any of the issues, either in favor of the plaintiff or defendant, and includes a verdict wherein the jury returns a finding of the plaintiff's total damages and assesses percentages of fault. A special verdict is one by which the jury finds the facts only, leaving the judgment to the court.

#### Committee Note – 1959

This Rule is the same as Section 106 of the 1943 Code (Section 510.220, RSMo 1959).

(Amended October 16, 1986, effective July 1, 1987.)

norms.heading: Jury Shall Render General Verdict – When

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 71 — Verdicts

norms.text:
In every issue for the recovery of money only, or specific real or personal property, the jury shall render a general verdict.

#### Committee Note – 1959

This Rule is the same as Section 107 of the 1943 Code (Section 510.230, RSMo 1959).

This rule is the same as original proposed Rule 22.02(a). Paragraph (b) of the proposed Rule 22.02 provided for a discretionary special verdict in the form of special findings on each issue of fact, and for submission to a jury of special interrogatories. Paragraph (b) is omitted for these reasons: (1) it is a radical change in the existing practice; (2) experience with similar provisions has not been uniformly satisfactory; (3) the Bar overwhelmingly opposed the discretionary special verdict system in all cases.

norms.heading: Jury Shall Assess Amount of Recovery, When

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 71 — Verdicts

norms.text:
When a verdict shall be found for the plaintiff in an action for the recovery of money only, the jury shall also assess the amount of recovery; so, also, if they find for the defendant in case of a counterclaim, crossclaim or other demand for money. A verdict shall meet the requirements of this rule if the jury returns a finding of the total amount of the damages and assesses percentages of fault.
When exemplary or punitive damages are allowed by the jury, the amount thereof shall be separately stated in the verdict. When both damages for personal injuries and damages to property are allowed by the jury, the verdict shall state separately the amount allowed for the aggregate of the items of damage connected with the personal injury and the amount allowed for the aggregate of the items of damage connected with the injury to the property.

#### Committee Note – 1959

This Rule is Section 111 of the 1943 Code (Section 510.270, RSMo 1959) with a new sentence added and provision made for counter-claims and cross-claims instead of "offsets." ... This new sentence provides that the damages for personal injury and property damage be stated separately in the verdict. This will be of great help in cases involving subrogation rights and in tax computations.

norms.heading: Motion for a Directed Verdict and for Judgment Notwithstanding the Verdict

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 72 — Motion for a Directed Verdict and for Judgment Notwithstanding the Verdict

norms.text:
(a) Motion for Directed Verdict: When Made: Effect. A party may move for a directed verdict at the close of the evidence offered by an opponent. The filing of such motion does not constitute a waiver of movant's right to offer evidence to the same extent as if the motion had not been made. A motion which is not granted is not a waiver of trial by jury even though all parties to the action have moved for directed verdicts. A motion for a directed verdict shall state the specific grounds therefor. The order of the court granting a motion for a directed verdict is effective without any assent of the jury.
(b) Motion for Judgment Notwithstanding the Verdict. A party may move for a directed verdict at the close of all the evidence. Whenever such motion is denied or for any reason is not granted, the court is deemed to have submitted the action to the jury subject to a later determination of the legal questions raised by the motion.
Not later than thirty days after entry of judgment, a party who has moved for a directed verdict may move to have the verdict and any judgment entered thereon set aside and to have judgment entered in accordance with the motion for a directed verdict; or if a verdict was not returned, such party, within thirty days after the jury has been discharged, may move for judgment in accordance with the motion for a directed verdict.
A motion for a new trial may be joined with this motion, or a new trial may be prayed for in the alternative. If a verdict was returned the court may allow the judgment to stand or may reopen the judgment and either order a new trial or direct the entry of judgment as if the requested verdict had been directed. If no verdict was returned the court may direct the entry of judgment as if the requested verdict had been directed or may order a new trial.
(c) Same: Conditional Rulings on Grant of Motion.
(1) If the motion for judgment notwithstanding the verdict provided for in subdivision (b) of this Rule, is granted, the court shall also rule on the motion for a new trial, if any, by determining whether it should be granted if the judgment is thereafter vacated or reversed, and shall specify the grounds for granting or denying the motion for the new trial.
If the motion for a new trial is thus conditionally granted, the order thereon does not affect the finality of the judgment. In case the motion for a new trial has been conditionally granted and the judgment is reversed on appeal, the new trial shall proceed unless the appellate court has otherwise ordered. In case the motion for new trial has been conditionally denied, the respondent on appeal may assert error in that denial; and if the judgment is reversed on appeal, subsequent proceedings shall be in accordance with the order of the appellate court.
(2) The party whose judgment has been set aside on the motion for judgment notwithstanding verdict, may upon appeal from the resulting adverse judgment, in addition to urging that the trial court erred in sustaining the motion for judgment notwithstanding the verdict, also brief and argue and the appellate court may determine, whether the appellant is, in any event, entitled to a new trial.
(d) Same: Denial of Motion. If the motion for judgment notwithstanding the verdict is denied, the party who prevailed on that motion, as respondent, may assert grounds entitling the party to a new trial in the event the appellate court concludes that the trial court erred in denying the motion for judgment notwithstanding the verdict. If the appellate court reverses the judgment, nothing in this Rule 72.01 precludes it from determining that the respondent is entitled to a new trial or from directing the court to determine whether a new trial shall be granted.

norms.heading: Trial Without Jury or With an Advisory Jury – Procedures

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 73 — Trial by Court

norms.text:
In cases tried without a jury or with an advisory jury:

(a) The court shall rule upon all objections to evidence as in jury cases. Where the evidence is ruled inadmissible, the court upon request shall take and record the evidence in full, unless it clearly appears that the evidence is not admissible on any ground or that the evidence is privileged.
(b) After the plaintiff has completed presentation of plaintiff's evidence, the defendant may move by motion for a judgment on the grounds that upon the facts and the law the plaintiff is not entitled to relief. The filing of such motion does not constitute a waiver of defendant's right to offer evidence.

(c) The court shall render the judgment it thinks proper under the law and the evidence.
If a party so requests, the court shall dictate to the court reporter or prepare and file a brief opinion containing a statement of the grounds for its decision and the method of deciding any damages awarded.

The court may, or if requested by a party shall, include in the opinion findings on the controverted material fact issues specified by the party. Any request for an opinion or findings of fact shall be made on the record before the introduction of evidence at trial or at such later time as the court may allow.
All fact issues upon which no specific findings are made shall be considered as having been found in accordance with the result reached.

(d) Except as provided in Rule 78.07(c), a party may, but need not, file a motion for new trial or a motion to amend the judgment or opinion, or both, as provided by Rule 78.04.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article confie au juge la décision sur le faux, tout en permettant de statuer séparément sur les autres chefs de demande. Les règles du Missouri prévoient le jugement selon le droit et la preuve ainsi que les jugements portant sur certaines demandes seulement, sans règle spécifique sur le faux documentaire.
correspondences.note_en: The article assigns the forgery issue to the judge while allowing the remaining claims to be decided separately. Missouri rules address judgment under the law and evidence and judgments on fewer than all claims, but contain no specific rule for documentary forgery.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet aux deux époux de demander expressément et conjointement que le juge n’énonce pas leurs torts et griefs dans les motifs, celui-ci constatant seulement les faits constitutifs d’une cause de divorce. Les §§ 452.320 et 452.305 imposent une constatation judiciaire du caractère irrémédiablement rompu du mariage et, le cas échéant, de faits justificatifs, sans prévoir cette dispense conjointe ; la Rule 73.01 concerne plus généralement les motifs et constatations du jugement.
correspondences.note_en: The article allows both spouses expressly and jointly to ask the judge not to state their faults and grievances in the reasoning, limiting the decision to finding facts constituting grounds for divorce. Sections 452.320 and 452.305 require findings that the marriage is irretrievably broken and, where applicable, supporting facts, but provide no comparable joint waiver; Rule 73.01 addresses opinions and factual findings more generally.

norms.heading: Judgment

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Governing Civil Procedure in the Circuit Courts
Rule 74 — Judgments, Orders and Proceedings Thereon

norms.text:
(a) Included Matters. "Judgment" as used in these rules includes a decree and any order from which an appeal lies. A judgment is rendered when entered. A judgment is entered when a writing signed by the judge and denominated "judgment" or "decree" is filed. The judgment may be a separate document or entry on the docket sheet of the case. A docket sheet entry complying with these requirements is a judgment unless the docket sheet entry indicates that the court will enter the judgment in a separate document. The separate document shall be the judgment when entered.
(b) Judgment Upon Multiple Claims or Involving Multiple Parties. When more than one claim for relief is presented in an action, whether as a claim, counterclaim, cross-claim, or third-party claim, or when multiple parties are involved, the court may enter a judgment as to one or more but fewer than all of the claims or parties only upon an express determination that there is no just reason for delay.
In the absence of such determination, any order or other form of decision, however designated, that adjudicates fewer than all the claims or the rights and liabilities of fewer than all the parties shall not terminate the action as to any of the claims or parties, and the order or other form of decision is subject to revision at any time before the entry of judgment adjudicating all the claims and the rights and liabilities of all the parties.
